papers.title: Defining the Antigenic Topology and Prospective Binding Breadth of Vaccination-induced SARS-CoV-2 Neutralizing Antibodies
papers.authors: Jaiswal, D.; Altomare, C. G.; Adelsberg, D. C.; Sapse, I. A.; Singh, G.; Krammer, F.; Simon, V.; Ellebedy, A. H.; Bajic, G.
papers.abstract: Antibodies that neutralize SARS-CoV-2 primarily target the viral spike glycoprotein, yet the breadth of these responses is continually challenged by viral evolution. While extensive structural studies have defined epitopes across the spike protein, how antibodies elicited by the initial mRNA vaccination campaigns perform against subsequently emerging variants remains an important question.Here, we structurally and functionally characterize a panel of early plasmablast-derived human monoclonal antibodies isolated following primary mRNA vaccination, targeting both the receptor-binding domain (RBD) and the N-terminal domain (NTD) of spike. Using cryo-electron microscopy, variant-binding analyses, and viral-fusion inhibition assays, we observe that antibodies directed against immunodominant regions of the RBD and NTD are highly potent but more frequently impacted by variant-associated mutations. In contrast, antibodies engaging a conserved hydrophobic pocket within the NTD exhibit broader reactivity and neutralize through distinct molecular mechanisms. Together, these findings extend prior structural studies of spike-directed antibodies by prospectively assessing the breadth of vaccine-elicited antibodies against later variants and identifying structural features associated with differential escape sensitivity. These results contribute to a growing understanding of how early vaccine-induced antibody repertoires relate to subsequent viral evolution.

papers.title: HIV broadly neutralizing antibody precursor maturation induced by mRNA vaccination in nonhuman primates
papers.authors: Phung, I.; Freeman, B. L.; Liguori, A.; Seymour, A.; Xie, Z.; Phulera, S.; Kalyuzhniy, O.; Madden, P. J.; Marina-Zarate, E.; Willis, J. R.; Cottrell, C. A.; Ma, K. M.; Baboo, S.; Flynn, C. T.; Kifude, C.; Lu, D.; Phelps, N.; Goodwin, D.; Adachi, Y.; Tingle, R.; Georgeson, E.; Tran, J.; Kalyuzhniy, A.; Hu, X.; Lewis, V. R.; Ngo, J. T.; Liu, X.; Diedrich, J. K.; Nair, U.; Himansu, S.; Schiffner, T.; Lusso, P.; Paulson, J. C.; Yates, J. R.; Carnathan, D. G.; Burton, D. R.; Irvine, D. J.; Silvestri, G.; Ward, A. B.; Ozorowski, G.; Batista, F. D.; Ramezani-Rad, P.; Steichen, J. M.; Crotty, S.; Schi
papers.abstract: The induction of broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) is a principal goal of prophylactic HIV vaccines. For many bnAbs, priming ultrarare precursors from the naive B cell repertoire is the first major immunological hurdle. Previous studies have shown that the germline-targeting (GT) priming immunogen N332-GT5 delivered as adjuvanted protein to non-human primates (NHPs) activates bnAb precursor B cells for the human bnAb BG18 targeting the V3-glycan supersite on the HIV envelope (Env) glycoprotein. Here, we engineered N332-GT6 to improve binding affinity to diverse BG18-class precursor naive B cells by 9-fold. mRNA-LNP vaccines expressing N332-GT5 or N332-GT6 as membrane-bound (gp151) trimers were evaluated for their ability to prime BG18-class precursor B cells in NHPs across three related studies. Although N332-GT5 gp151 mRNA-LNP priming induced BG18-class precursor B cells in most animals after two vaccinations, the higher-affinity N332-GT6 gp151 induced responses more consistently after only one immunization. Sequential vaccination with two heterologous mRNA-LNP booster immunizations drove affinity maturation and induced BG18-class memory B cells capable of binding wildtype HIV Env. Together, these findings demonstrate that mRNA immunization can achieve GT priming, boosting, and early maturation of ultrarare bnAb-class B cells in NHPs.

papers.title: Cross-cohort optimal transport maps macrophage plasticity and routes to inflammation and fibrosis in human atherosclerosis
papers.authors: Vazquez Montes de Oca, S.; Acedo Terrades, A.; Carreno Martinez, J. F.; Kirchner, P.; Ord, T.; Kaikkonen, M. U.; Siting, W.; Freigang, S. B.; Zlobec, I.; Rodriguez Martinez, M.
papers.abstract: Single-cell transcriptomics has revealed extensive macrophage heterogeneity in atherosclerotic plaques, but how disease-associated programs reshape cellular identity remains unclear. Connecting macrophage states to these molecular changes could help identify candidate routes through which macrophages contribute to inflammation and fibrosis. We developed a computational method combining optimal transport, RNA velocity and comparative program analysis across 34,533 monocytes and macrophages from seven human cohorts. Optimal transport quantified all 15 pairwise relationships among six macrophage states, and target-association gradients supported source- and destination-program comparisons across 11 relationships. Expression contrasts were calculated within libraries and source subtypes. Robustness was assessed through resampling, cohort omission and held-out-gene analyses. Paired RNA and protein measurements provided complementary molecular evidence, and patient-label permutation tests evaluated exploratory clinical associations in 18 patients. We also applied the method to an independent human liver dataset. Scavenging and inflammatory macrophages formed the closest transcriptional pair in the full atlas and every cohort-omission analysis. Scavenging macrophages retained selected source features alongside inflammatory programming, whereas fibrotic association coincided with attenuation of the broader scavenging signature. This signature showed a lower change along fibrotic than inflammatory association in all 19 matched libraries. Protein measurements corroborated selected changes and revealed coexisting scavenging and activation features within individual cells. Symptomatic patients had a higher fraction of monocytes with strong inflammatory association than asymptomatic patients (median difference, 13.0 percentage points; unadjusted one-sided permutation $p = 0.0017$). Analysis of 8,536 liver mononuclear phagocytes further resolved contrasting source-marker responses along scar-associated macrophage association. These findings connect macrophage heterogeneity to selective identity remodeling across disease-associated states. Integrating population relationships with RNA, protein and clinical measurements provides a strategy for prioritizing candidate pathogenic routes and their associated molecular programs for functional investigation.

papers.title: B cells dominate the heart immune infiltrate during chronic infectious cardiomyopathy
papers.authors: Dabek, A.; Fortes Francisco, A.; Khan, A. A.; Ashraf, S.; Dey, S.; Van Bocxlaer, K.; Ashwin, H.; Parker, K.; Dey, N. S.; Bayraktar, O. A.; Teichmann, S. A.; Taylor, M. C.; Green, E. A.; Kaye, P. M.; Kelly, J. M.; Lewis, M. D.; Perez-Mazliah, D.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in single-cell and spatially resolved multi-omics have revolutionised our understanding of the cellular and molecular niches governing cardiac homeostasis and acute injury. However, the immune-stromal networks sustaining long-term, chronic heart pathology remain poorly defined, largely due to a paucity of physiologically relevant experimental models. Here, through a side-by-side multi-omic comparison of Trypanosoma cruzi-infected mouse models displaying contrasting degrees of chronic myocardial pathology and fibrosis, we define the long-term cellular landscape of the inflamed fibrotic heart. We reveal that class-switched, antibody-secreting plasma B cells represent the predominant immune subset infiltrating the fibrotic myocardium. CellChat intercellular communication modelling identifies plasma cell-fibroblast crosstalk as the strongest immune-stromal interaction in the fibrosis-prone heart, driven by predicted matrix anchoring (CD44-collagen/laminin) and molecular survival axes (App-Cd74, C3-Cr2). Supporting these computational predictions, immunofluorescence and spatial profiling confirm close proximity between plasma B cells and fibroblasts, alongside a striking accumulation of B cells embedded within extracellular matrix-rich cardiac scars. This localised B cell response maintains prominent pools of parasite-reactive and heart-autoreactive antibody-secreting cells despite a lack of detectable parasite signal in their immediate micro-vicinity. Together, these findings identify a matrix-associated plasma B cell-fibroblast niche as a central driver of chronic cardiac remodelling, revealing how persistent tissue scarring can become decoupled from direct local pathogen presence.

papers.title: Towards a best-in-class IgE disruptor for food allergy with Claude-enabled antibody design
papers.authors: Erives, E.; Ferrara, E.; Michael, S.; Mallipeddi, N.; Jing, B.
papers.abstract: Food allergy affects an estimated 220-250 million people worldwide, for whom the constant risk of a severe reaction weighs heavily on quality of life. Allergic reactions are triggered by the cross-linking of allergen-specific IgE bound to its high-affinity receptor, Fc{epsilon}RI, on mast cells and basophils, causing degranulation, inflammation and, in severe cases, anaphylaxis. Omalizumab (Xolair), the sole FDA-approved biologic for food allergy, neutralizes circulating IgE; however, it does not effectively remove IgE from Fc{epsilon}RI, where it can persist for weeks and where even a small residual amount can sustain sensitivity. Here we describe an agentic computational design campaign with Claude toward a disruptive inhibitor antibody that physically removes bound IgE from Fc{epsilon}RI. Guided by our research team, Claude pursued a biparatopic molecule that pairs a disruptor arm, which displaces IgE from Fc{epsilon}RI, with a non-competing anchor arm that holds the molecule on receptor-bound IgE. Of 91 experimentally characterized disruptor designs, 20 showed activity against receptor-bound IgE by competitive bio-layer interferometry, and in a dose-titration assay three variants removed more IgE than omalizumab at therapeutically relevant concentrations (25-400 nM). De novo designs for the anchor arm bound IgE at diverse epitopes with apparent affinities of 3.4-235 nM. These subcomponents provide the starting point for further characterization toward a best-in-class IgE disruptor.

papers.title: Structural and functional characterization of polyclonal antibody responses reveals shared and distinct antigenic features of RSV and hMPV fusion proteins
papers.authors: Bermudez-Mendez, E.; Ols, S.; Cufaro, L. V.; Xiao, S.; Peng, Z.; Gegenfurtner, F.; Eray, E. R.; Miranda, M. C.; Arcoverde Cerveira, R.; Segura Garcia, M.; Veliz Pernilla, M. A.; Hanke, L.; Borst, A. J.; King, N. P.; Antanasijevic, A.; Lore, K.
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV), members of the Pneumoviridae family, circulate widely and are leading causes of hospitalization for acute respiratory infections in infants and older adults. The viral fusion (F) protein in its prefusion (preF) conformation is the primary target of neutralizing antibodies, yet how naturally elicited circulating polyclonal antibodies are distributed across its antigenic landscape remains poorly understood. Here, we combined serological profiling, site-specific antibody competition assays and electron microscopy-based polyclonal epitope mapping (EMPEM) to characterize preF-directed immunity to RSV and hMPV in healthy adults. All donors exhibited detectable preF-binding antibodies that positively correlated with virus neutralization and broadly recognized multiple antigenic sites, consistent with immunodominance patterns predicted by a surface-centric computational model. Despite this overall similarity, the distribution of responses across individual antigenic sites differed between RSV and hMPV. EMPEM analyses revealed consistent targeting of the highly neutralization-sensitive preF apex (site O) in both viruses, alongside less abundant responses against equatorial and upper-middle epitopes (sites II, III, IV and V). We additionally observed antibody-bound destabilized preF, supporting a model in which antibody binding promotes transient opening of the preF trimer and may interfere with the conformational rearrangements required for membrane fusion. Together, these findings highlight apex-directed antibodies as a prominent feature of naturally acquired pneumovirus immunity in adults and reveal both shared and distinct patterns of antigenic recognition that may inform next-generation vaccine design and antibody-based prophylactics.

papers.title: Single-cell metabolic profiling reveals time-associated metabolic trajectories linked to functional changes in anti-tumor NK cells.
papers.authors: Qiao H, Cheng S, Feng L, Tan S, Gong X, Shentu X.
papers.abstract: Cellular metabolism shapes immune-cell function, yet single-cell metabolic heterogeneity remains analytically challenging to resolve. Here, we applied label-free cytometry by electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (CyESI-MS) to NK-92MI, a human natural killer (NK) cell line. Cells were collected from a NK-92MI/HeLa co-culture model at 0 h (resting condition), 6 h (early activation condition), and 72 h (prolonged stimulation condition). The 0 h condition was characterized by baseline cytotoxicity, low interferon gamma (IFN-γ) production, and minimal programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) expression. The 6 h condition was characterized by peak cytotoxicity and increased IFN-γ production. The 72 h condition was characterized by reduced cytotoxicity and IFN-γ production relative to their 6 h peaks, together with increased PD-1 expression. Single-cell metabolic profiling revealed time-associated metabolic trajectories linked to these functional changes. Across the dataset, 158 metabolite features were detected. The early activation condition showed changes consistent with antioxidant, central carbon/amino-acid, and lipid remodeling. In contrast, the prolonged stimulation condition showed broader metabolic imbalance. Together, these findings establish a proof-of-concept framework for linking single-cell metabolic trajectories with independently measured changes in NK-cell function.

papers.title: Use of Antibody Structural Information in Disease Prediction Models Reveals Antigen Specific B Cell Receptor Sequences in Bulk Repertoire Data
papers.authors: Nwogu, O.; Gill, K. K.; Moore, C.; Kroner, J. W.; Chang, W.-C.; Burkle, J.; Stevens, M. L.; Baatyrbek kyzy, A.; Miraldi, E. R.; Biagini, J. M.; Devonshire, A. L.; Kottyan, L.; Schwartz, J. T.; Assa'ad, A. H.; Martin, L. J.; Andorf, S.; Hershey, G. K. K.; Roskin, K. M.
papers.abstract: Convergent antibodies are highly similar antibodies elicited in multiple individuals in response to the same antigen. Convergent antibodies provide insight into shared immunological responses and show great promise as diagnostic biomarkers. They have typically been identified using methods that consider the amino acid sequence of the third complementarity-determining region (CDR3) of immunoglobulin heavy chain (IgH). In this study, we extend this definition of convergent antibodies to use structural information about the three IgH CDR regions (CDR1-3) and antibody isotype. We measure the performance of both definitions of convergence by their ability to predict disease status from bulk IgH sequencing data for two different disease cohorts: HIV infection and food allergen sensitization. We show that using predicted structural information outperforms prior approaches for the prediction of food sensitization status and performs on par for HIV infection status. Additionally, the use of structural information and antibody isotype enables better model interpretation and more immunological insights. The structurally convergent antibody groups driving HIV prediction accuracy are from known HIV-binding antibodies expressing the appropriate isotype. Thus, the incorporation of structural information can enable the identification of antigen specific antibody groups from bulk IgH sequencing data.

papers.title: In situ profiling of plasma cell clonality with image-based single-cell transcriptomics.
papers.authors: Yang E, Aceves-Salvador J, Castrillon C, Herrmann US, Akama-Garren EH, Carroll MC, Moffitt JR.
papers.abstract: Image-based single-cell transcriptomics can identify diverse cell types in intact tissues. However, in adaptive immunity, V(D)J recombination generates unique immune receptors in cells of the same type, leading to important functional variation that is not yet defined by these methods. Here we introduce B cell receptor multiplexed error-robust fluorescence in situ hybridization (BCR-MERFISH), which measures plasma cell clonality based on V gene usage in combination with transcriptome profiling. We demonstrate that BCR-MERFISH accurately identifies V gene usage in cell culture and in mice with restricted or native plasma cell diversity. We then use BCR-MERFISH to elucidate the microbiota-dependent changes in plasma cell abundance, clonal diversity, and public clonotype usage in the mouse gut and the non-uniform distribution of plasma cell clones along the mouse ileum. Given that tissue context is an essential modulator of plasma cell dynamics, we anticipate that BCR-MERFISH may offer new insights into a wide range of immunological questions.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptomic profiling of PM2.5 ovarian toxicity: pulmonary particulate instillation associates with leukocyte infiltration and impaired granulosa cholesterol biosynthesis.
papers.authors: Zhang L, Zheng Y, Shi X, Li N, Tian J, Duan S.
papers.abstract: Ambient fine particulate matter (PM2.5) exposure impairs female reproductive capacity and accelerates follicular depletion, yet ovarian responses remain poorly illustrated at single-cell resolution. To evaluate early multicellular alterations following exposure, we combined a mouse model of repeated pulmonary PM2.5 instillation with single-cell transcriptomic profiling and in situ histological validation. We found that pulmonary PM2.5 instillation expanded the ovarian immune compartment through B-lineage lymphocyte and neutrophil infiltration, whereas resident macrophages adopted a C1qa-enriched scavenger profile without canonical NLRP3 inflammasome activation. At the intercellular interface, immune-derived TGF-β1 and TNF signals engaged somatic receptors and elevated downstream JAK-STAT pathway activity across recipient ovarian somatic cells. Specifically, in follicular granulosa cells, immune-somatic signaling suppressed the cholesterol-biosynthesis program independently of autonomous inflammatory stress, accompanied by matrix remodeling in stromal fibroblasts. Furthermore, dynamic trajectory modeling and in silico perturbation prioritized STAT1 as a candidate regulator of follicular deviation toward atretic fates. Concordantly, in situ multiplex immunofluorescence, TUNEL, and immunohistochemical assays verified parenchymal leukocyte localization, somatic Phospho-STAT1 nuclear engagement, preserved granulosa HMGCR expression, and follicular granulosa apoptosis in intact ovaries. In summary, our findings indicate that pulmonary PM2.5 instillation disrupts ovarian homeostasis through leukocyte infiltration, granulosa sterol suppression, and STAT1-associated follicular atresia.

papers.title: CD74 links MHC class II risk to tumor immune microenvironment remodeling across the Sjögren-to-lymphoma axis.
papers.authors: Liu S, Li M, Wang Y, Xia X, Wang P, Ni Z, Li Q, Teng Q, Han W, Liu J, Wang X, Yu S, Zhang H, Meng X, Zhong F, Wang H.
papers.abstract: Sjögren's syndrome creates a lymphoma-prone inflammatory niche and confers one of the highest autoimmune risks of B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma. Yet the genetic and cellular mechanisms that remodel this pre-neoplastic niche into a tumor-supportive immune microenvironment remain unclear. We integrated human genetics, single-cell transcriptomics and functional cell biology to identify an actionable mediator of this transition. We combined bidirectional Mendelian randomization, directionality filtering, MHC-exclusion sensitivity analyses (chromosome 6: 25-35 Mb), colocalization and summary-based HLA fine-mapping. Single-cell RNA sequencing of salivary gland and splenic marginal-zone lymphoma was used to localize genetic risk, reconstruct cross-disease B-cell states and infer intercellular signaling. Mechanistic dependence was tested in IFN-γ-stimulated Raji B-lymphoma cells, and clinical relevance was evaluated in a public chronic lymphocytic leukemia cohort. Genetic liability to Sjögren's syndrome increased marginal-zone/MALT, diffuse large B-cell and overall non-Hodgkin lymphoma risk, and effects collapsed after MHC exclusion and resolved to the class II 8.1 ancestral haplotype. Single-cell analysis localized risk to salivary B cells and revealed disease-associated remodeling toward a lymphoid, MIF-rich, CD74-receiving microenvironment, with plasma cells as the largest MIF source. HLA-class-II/CD74 programs increased along the Sjögren-to-lymphoma B-cell trajectory. In Raji cells, MIF activated AKT/NF-κB/BCL-xL signaling and viability. ISO-1 or CD74 knockdown suppressed the pathway and increased cleaved PARP, whereas AKT activation partially rescued signaling and viability. Higher CD74 expression marked adverse outcome in an external B-cell malignancy cohort. Convergent genetic, single-cell and perturbation evidence positions CD74 as a candidate organizer of a lymphoma-supportive immune microenvironment linking inherited MHC class II risk to B-cell survival. The MIF-CD74 axis provides a translational tumor-microenvironment target that requires tissue-level and prospective validation.

papers.title: The Immune Epitope Database (IEDB) in 2026: updates of immune receptor data.
papers.authors: Scheffer L, Richardson EM, Vita R, Zarebski L, Blazeska N, Wheeler DK, Cantrell JR, Greenbaum JA, Marrama D, Duesing S, Carri I, Nymann Deleuran S, Lees WD, Christley S, Corrie B, Cowell LG, Sette A, Peters B.
papers.abstract: The Immune Epitope Database (IEDB, iedb.org) is a freely available resource cataloging experimentally defined immune epitopes and, where reported, the immune receptors that recognize them. The IEDB currently records ∼235 000 distinct T cell receptors and ∼6400 distinct B cell receptors/antibodies with experimentally verified epitope specificity. Here, we describe recent updates to the IEDB, centered on a comprehensive revision of these receptor data. Because receptors were curated from 3879 references spanning decades, heterogeneity in gene nomenclature and CDR delimitation presents challenges for computational analyses and user queries. We rebuilt the standardization and validation pipeline to compute IUIS/IMGT-compliant V/D/J gene names and consistently delimited V domain, CDR1, 2, 3, and Junction sequences, and identify anomalous receptors from 822 references for re-curation. The IEDB web interface was expanded to include receptor search features directly on the homepage, support V/J gene and species options in the refined receptor search, and direct data export in the Adaptive Immune Receptor Repertoire (AIRR) format. We anticipate that the improved data quality will simplify bioinformatics analyses and facilitate integration into cross-repository data resources, such as the AIRR Knowledge Commons.

papers.title: Treatment standard - the highly sensitized kidney transplant candidate.
papers.authors: Martinez-Lacalle A, Meneghini M, Kervella D, Moreso F, Bestard O.
papers.abstract: Highly sensitized kidney transplant candidates are exposed to prolonged dialysis time and limited access to transplantation despite significant advances in allocation. Conventional desensitization therapies have shown limited efficacy in reducing circulating HLA antibodies, most often being incomplete or transient, reflecting the persistence of humoral alloimmune memory. Long-lived plasma cells, memory B cells and their supporting T-cell networks represent key cellular reservoirs sustaining or rapidly restoring HLA antibodies. A deeper understanding of these cellular reservoirs is now driving a shift in desensitization strategies. Rather than relying solely on antibody removal or depletion of a single cell population, emerging approaches seek to disrupt humoral immunity at multiple, complementary levels. Rapid IgG degradation with imlifidase can overcome immediate antibody barriers, while CD38-targeted therapies and rational combinations targeting both peripheral memory B cells and bone marrow-resident long-lived plasma cells (LLPC) with distinct targeted therapies aim to remodel the underlying antibody-producing compartment. At the same time, immune-engineering approaches, including chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cells and bispecific T cell engagers, are opening new possibilities for profound depletion of B-cell and plasma-cell populations. More radical strategies, such as nonmyeloablative autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, seek to reset rather than simply suppress the immune repertoire, while emerging HLA-directed platforms may ultimately enable selective targeting of alloimmune memory. Together, these developments mark a shift from transient antibody reduction towards deeper and potentially durable remodeling of humoral alloimmune memory. The ultimate challenge is to achieve sufficient HLA-specific immune control to enable transplantation while minimizing the consequences of broad immune depletion.

papers.title: Current Evidence of Precision Medicine via Multi-Omic Approaches in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
papers.authors: Leoni ER, Abbenante ED, Contrera KJ, Unrue KC, Hanania AN, Kansara SG.
papers.abstract: Perioperative and adjuvant immunotherapy are new standards of care for selected patients with resectable locoregionally advanced HPV-negative HNSCC, but low pathologic response rates and a lack of predictive biomarkers limit patient selection and response-adapted care. This review examines multi-omic approaches to predicting immunotherapy response and personalizing therapy. A narrative review of current multi-omic strategies for HNSCC was performed. Data providing predictive, prognostic, diagnostic, surveillance, or exploratory value was summarized. Multi-omics may identify those likely to benefit from immunotherapy. Single-cell transcriptomics reveals changes in the tumor immune microenvironment while spatial proteomics reveals tertiary lymphoid structures, dendritic cell networks, and protein signatures predicting immunotherapy response. Obstacles include unstandardized protocols, limited prospective validation, and small sample sizes. Multi-omics can reshape biomarker-driven HNSCC care, but implementation requires prospective validation, standardized protocols, and multi-platform integration.

papers.title: Association of dietary fiber intake with stroke history and characterization of a stroke related five gene immune signature: an exploratory study.
papers.authors: Zhang C, Zhang J.
papers.abstract: Dietary fiber intake has been associated with cerebrovascular health, motivating investigation of its relationship with inflammation and stroke-related immune expression. We combined NHANES population analyses with whole blood microarray and single-cell transcriptomic analyses to examine dietary associations and characterize a stroke-related gene signature. NHANES analyses included 34,928 adults from 2005 to 2018, including 1,348 with self-reported stroke history. Associations were examined using fully adjusted survey-weighted logistic regression, with a sensitivity analysis using two-day mean intake. Candidate genes were selected using GSE16561 and external gene resources, followed by LASSO selection and external validation in 46 GSE58294 participants. Single-cell analysis included 91,176 cells from three paired donors. Each unit increase in ln(fiber intake + 0.1) was associated with an odds ratio of 0.755 (95% confidence interval 0.663 to 0.861) for stroke history. Analysis of two-day mean intake showed a consistent association, with an odds ratio of 0.601 (0.499 to 0.723). Higher fiber intake was also associated with lower NLR, MLR, SIRI, and CRP levels. Of 15 candidate genes, LASSO retained CD163, PAK1, FOS, PTGS2, and HDAC4. The model achieved an external area under the curve of 0.964 (0.916 to 1.000). Single-cell analysis localized CD163, PAK1, and PTGS2 predominantly to monocytes and conventional dendritic cells. FOS showed broad expression, whereas HDAC4 was relatively enriched in naive CD4 T cells. These findings identify inverse associations of dietary fiber intake with stroke history and systemic inflammatory markers, together with a discriminative five-gene blood signature and its cellular distribution, providing directions for further investigation of nutritional and immune processes in stroke.

papers.title: Ferroptosis-associated macrophages suggest a potential ACSL1-PGE2-stromal iron homeostasis-related axis in endometriosis.
papers.authors: Wang J, Liu M, Luo X, Zhang Y, Ding J.
papers.abstract: Endometriosis (EMs) is characterized by chronic inflammation, recurrent bleeding, oxidative stress, and disrupted local iron homeostasis. Although macrophages are important components of the immune microenvironment in EMs, their ferroptosis-related heterogeneity and potential association with iron homeostasis remain unclear. This study investigated ferroptosis-associated macrophages (FAMs) and their potential involvement in immune-iron homeostasis coupling in EMs. Publicly available single-cell RNA sequencing data were used to characterize macrophage heterogeneity in eutopic endometrial samples from women with EMs and disease-free controls. Differential expression, functional enrichment, donor-level, pseudobulk, pseudotime ordering, and inferred cell-cell communication analyses, together with independent bulk RNA sequencing, were used to prioritize candidate regulators. In vitro experiments included ferroptosis-related phenotype induction, ACSL1 knockdown, PGE2 quantification, EP2 receptor blockade, and iron-loading and chelation assays. FAMs were preferentially enriched in the EMs group and exhibited elevated ferroptosis-related transcriptional activity. Integrative transcriptomic and donor-level analyses supported the prioritization of acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 1 (ACSL1) as a candidate metabolic regulator. Ferrostatin-1 treatment significantly attenuated erastin-induced lipid peroxidation and cellular injury. ACSL1 knockdown markedly attenuated ferroptosis-related alterations and PGE2 secretion in macrophages. In endometriotic stromal cells, PGE2 treatment downregulated FTH1 expression, upregulated SLC40A1 expression, and elevated extracellular Fe³⁺ levels; these changes were partially reversed by EP2 receptor blockade. Iron chelation treatment significantly attenuated FAC-induced lipid peroxidation and cellular injury in macrophages. The findings support a proposed macrophage-stromal interaction axis linking ACSL1-PGE2-associated signaling, stromal iron homeostasis-related changes, and extracellular iron loading, with potential intervention points involving ACSL1, PGE2/EP2 signaling, and iron homeostasis.

papers.title: Targeting lipid metabolism to overcome immunosuppression and enhance immunotherapy or chemotherapy sensitivity in pancreatic cancer: from immunosuppressive mechanisms to therapeutic opportunities.
papers.authors: Zhan T, Liu Y, Yan J, Huang X.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is characterized by immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME), in which immunosuppression and immune evasion lead to poor response to therapies. Lipid metabolism reprogramming is a central feature of PDAC progression and, depending on the lipid species and context, can promote immunosuppression and immune evasion. Here, we summarize the regulation of lipid metabolism in PDAC and the TME and highlight therapeutic targeting potential. KRAS mutations drive the abnormal activation of key molecules such as SREBP1, FASN, and CD36, promoting de novo fatty acid synthesis, cholesterol metabolism, and the uptake of extracellular lipids. Tumor cells evade immune surveillance by upregulating immune checkpoint molecules and suppressing antigen presentation, thereby impairing both innate and adaptive antitumor immunity. Lipid overload triggers lipid competition and lipotoxicity, induces CD8⁺ T-cell exhaustion and promotes the recruitment of immunosuppressive cells such as M2 macrophages and myeloid-derived suppressor cells. Pancreatic stellate cells and peritumoral adipocytes undergo profound lipid metabolic reprogramming and influence the lipid metabolism of PDAC cells and immune function through mechanisms such as paracrine signaling, thereby further reinforcing the immunosuppressive microenvironment. Lipid metabolism interventions such as targeting fatty acid synthesis, cholesterol metabolism, and lipid peroxidation-driven ferroptosis in combination with chemotherapy and/or immunotherapy have shown promise in preclinical models. Targeting lipid metabolism can reshape the immunosuppressive microenvironment and enhance the sensitivity to PD-1 blockade and gemcitabine, significantly improving antitumor efficacy. In the future, combining spatial metabolomics and single cell lipidomics may reveal the interactions between lipid metabolism and the immune system and explore the mechanisms underlying the lipid metabolic interaction networks among tumor-immune-and stromal cells.

papers.title: FGD5-AS1/miR-106b-5p/FDX1 axis governs cuproptosis to affect clear cell renal cell carcinoma progression via metabolic-immune crosstalk.
papers.authors: Tang F, Wang W, Chang Y, Gu Y, Wei X, Ren Y, Ouyang Y, Zhang S.
papers.abstract: Inactive cuproptosis has been linked to the progression of clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC); however, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, a cuproptosis-related scoring system, termed the cuproptosis suppression score (CSS) was developed based on multiple cuproptosis-related genes. Single-cell RNA-sequencing data were employed to examine the correlations between the CSS and the immune landscape and metabolic reprogramming. Luciferase reporter assays and in vitro functional experiments were conducted to analyze the potential competitive endogenous RNA mechanism regulating FDX1 expression and to evaluate the functional effects of FDX1 in ccRCC development. We observed that the CSS was inversely correlated with the expression levels of cuproptosis-promoting genes. High-CSS tumor cells exhibited enrichment of the epithelial-mesenchymal transition, angiogenesis, and RTK/RAS pathways. Cuproptosis appeared to influence tumor progression by modulating metabolic reprogramming and remodeling the immune microenvironment, with cuproptosis-related intercellular and cytokine signaling potentially alleviating T cell exhaustion. Notably, the CSS accurately predicted immunotherapy responses. Furthermore, FDX1, a key cuproptosis regulator, was inversely linked to the CSS, and its upregulation suppressed ccRCC cell proliferation and migration. The lncRNA FGD5-AS1 upregulated FDX1 by sponging miR-106b-5p. Altogether, this study provides mechanistic insights into how cuproptosis may limit ccRCC progression, potentially through metabolic reprogramming and tumor immune escape. Cuproptosis-based anticancer strategies hold significant promise for integration into precision medicine in ccRCC.

papers.title: KCNQ3 as a pan-cancer prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target: Multi-omics profiling and mechanistic validation in cholangiocarcinoma.
papers.authors: Ma S, Liang Y, Zhang D, Chen Y, Wu Q, Liu H, Su Y, Zhong D, Wang M, Zou H, Lu Z, Huang X.
papers.abstract: Potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily Q member 3(KCNQ3) is essential for neuronal function; however, its expression and role in human cancers remain unexplored. A comprehensive pan-cancer multi-omics analysis was conducted utilizing GTEx, HPA, TIMER2, TISCH2, cBioPortal, SMART, and TIMER3 databases, in conjunction with single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses. In cholangiocarcinoma (CHOL) cells and in vivo mouse models, we performed functional assays to assess cell proliferation, apoptosis, migration, invasion, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), together with transcriptomic and molecular analyses, to elucidate the mechanisms mediated by KCNQ3. KCNQ3 exhibited tissue-specific expression and was upregulated in various malignancies, including breast cancer, CHOL, hepatocellular cancer, lung adenocarcinoma, thyroid carcinomas, among others. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses demonstrated its enrichment in malignant cells, monocytes/macrophages, fibroblasts, and endothelial cells. Pan-cancer profiling identified copy number amplification and promoter DNA hypomethylation as key epigenetic features. Elevated KCNQ3 levels were associated with poorer overall, progression-free, disease-specific, and disease-free survival across tumor types. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) linked KCNQ3 to epithelial-mesenchymal transition, inflammatory response, and KRAS signaling, while indicating reduction of oxidative phosphorylation and DNA repair. Immune analysis revealed positive correlations with myeloid-derived suppressor cells, M2 macrophages, and cancer-associated fibroblasts, and negative correlations with activated NK cells and CD8 + T cells. In CHOL, KCNQ3 knockdown inhibited proliferation, migration, invasion, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition, triggering apoptosis via ERK1/2 inhibition in vitro and in vivo. This study identifies KCNQ3 as a potential oncogenic driver that promotes progression through reprogramming, metabolic rewiring, and immune modulation, representing a promising prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target across malignancies.

papers.title: A tumor-responsive p53-loaded nanovesicle system for senescence induction and immune microenvironment reprogramming.
papers.authors: Guo Z, Gong Y, Chen J, Shen L, Wang W, Qi Q, Chi Y, Ma K, Ju H, Han Y.
papers.abstract: The tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) critically regulates the balance between antitumor immunity and immune evasion. Although cellular senescence can promote immune-mediated tumor clearance through the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), this mechanism is frequently compromised by loss of p53 function, particularly in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). Consequently, strategies capable of restoring p53 activity while harnessing intact immune-responsive pathways are urgently needed. Integrated transcriptomic analyses provided a computational basis for this therapeutic strategy. Bulk RNA-seq demonstrated that, in TNBC, the downstream SASP-immune activation axis remains largely preserved, whereas the upstream p53-SASP coupling is disrupted, supporting the concept that exogenous p53 restoration may effectively re-engage immune programs. Single-cell RNA-seq further revealed that p53-functional malignant cells exhibit enhanced tumor-immune communication and immune-recognition signals, reinforcing the feasibility of p53 reactivation to remodel the TIME. Guided by these insights, we engineered a dual-functional, tumor-responsive nanovesicle system for p53 delivery. Escherichia coli was genetically modified to express p53, and p53-loaded outer membrane vesicles (OMV@p53) were coated with a biomimetic calcium phosphate shell via bionanomorphic mineralization, yielding acid-responsive nanovesicles (Ca@OMV@p53; 200-300 nm). This coating enhanced biocompatibility and enabled pH-triggered release within the mildly acidic tumor microenvironment. In vitro, Ca@OMV@p53 efficiently induced tumor cell senescence and promoted M1 macrophage polarization. In vivo, treatment markedly increased intratumoral infiltration of M1 macrophages and cytotoxic T lymphocytes, accompanied by elevated pro-inflammatory cytokines and sustained immune activation. Together, this study demonstrates that p53-restoration via a tumor-responsive nanodelivery system can synergistically induce senescence and immune-mediated tumor clearance. By integrating systems-level bioinformatics with experimental nanomedicine, our work establishes a rational framework for senescence-based immunomodulatory cancer therapy.

papers.title: Collagen-PMMA scaffolds induce dermal remodeling and immune recruitment distinct from simple volar fibroblast therapy in human skin.
papers.authors: Lee SS, Xue Y, Li A, Haddad NR, Curvin-Aquilla L, Johnson A, Willis A, Lee JC, Kim J, Winnicki E, Ruci A, Sicilia I, Liu Z, Blumenthal J, Huang A, Won A, Qi J, Yu D, Park M, Kirby C, van Ee A, Minsky H, Garcia-Rodenas R, Jung E, Liu J, Garza LA.
papers.abstract: Cellular therapy is a promising modality but requires optimization in human subjects, particularly for solid organs. Volar skin of the palms and soles is adapted to mechanical stress through a thick epidermis and dense extracellular matrix. These features are reduced in non-volar skin, increasing vulnerability at high-pressure sites such as prosthetic limb interfaces. Volar fibroblasts can partially reprogram non-volar skin toward volar characteristics, suggesting a strategy to prevent pressure related injury. We tested whether combining volar fibroblast therapy with a collagen/polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) scaffold could enhance remodeling by providing additional niches for ectopic fibroblast engraftment. Healthy volunteers received injections of vehicle, scalp fibroblasts, or volar fibroblasts, with or without collagen/PMMA, into non-volar skin. Durometer, optical coherence tomography, and histology showed volar-like changes, including increased skin firmness, epidermal thickness, papillary elastin, and collagen fiber density after treatment. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics revealed activation of skin development, keratinocyte differentiation, extracellular matrix organization, and morphogenesis pathways. Collagen/PMMA promoted fibroblast, immune, and endothelial cell accumulation, consistent with a scaffold-associated tissue response across treatment groups. These findings distinguish volar fibroblast-associated changes in skin identity from collagen/PMMA-induced stromal remodeling, which includes features of a foreign body response and may contain inflammatory and fibrotic/myofibroblast-associated components.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics tumor microenvironment determinants of tyrosine kinase inhibitor response in renal cell carcinoma: results from a phase 2 clinical trial.
papers.authors: Hasanov E, Ali MIH, Deshmukh S, Ovando-Ricardez JA, Lam T, Hoang A, Liu XD, Wang X, Peterson CB, Xiao L, Matin SF, Sircar K, Tannir NM, Hasanov M, Jonasch E.
papers.abstract: Metastatic clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) exhibits heterogeneous clinical outcomes, and limited biomarkers are available to predict response to targeted therapies. This study evaluated cell compartment-specific transcriptional biomarkers predicting clinical response to the tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) sunitinib. In this phase 2 clinical trial (NCT00715442), 46 patients with metastatic ccRCC received sunitinib pre- and post-cytoreductive nephrectomy, with a primary endpoint of time-to-progression (TTP) and secondary endpoints of overall survival (OS) and sunitinib toxicity. To investigate spatial dynamics of therapeutic response to sunitinib, we applied whole-transcriptome digital spatial profiling (DSP) to tumor tissue from responders and non-responders. For 46 trial patients, median TTP was 8.2 months (95% CI: 6.1-19.3) and OS 36.3 months (95% CI: 19.7-70.5). Responders displayed a tumor microenvironment enriched in pro-inflammatory/immunostimulatory programs, while non-responders displayed enrichment of immunosuppressive programs with elevated PD-L1 expression in myeloid cells and exhausted CD8 + T-cell signatures. Sunitinib resistance mechanisms involving VEGF-dependent and independent angiogenic pathways were identified, revealing potential therapeutic targets. DSP-based machine learning models showed strong prognostic and predictive performance in sunitinib-treated patients in an external JAVELIN Renal 101 cohort, but attenuated performance in the avelumab plus axitinib cohort, indicating treatment-context specificity. Our findings highlight immune regulation as a key determinant of sunitinib response in metastatic ccRCC. Spatial profiling revealed potentially targetable mechanisms of TKI resistance involving SPP1-associated myeloid programs, CD8 + T-cell exhaustion, and angiogenic signaling, highlighting interactions between angiogenesis, lipid metabolism, and tumor immunity as determinants of therapeutic outcome.

papers.title: miR-155 expression associates with pathogenic circulating follicular helper T-cell phenotype in myasthenia gravis.
papers.authors: Ashida S, Ochi H, Fujii C, Hamatani M, Mizuno T, Kondo T.
papers.abstract: Introduction Myasthenia gravis (MG) is an antibody-mediated autoimmune disease targeting neuromuscular junctions. We previously reported that ICOS-high expressing circulating follicular T cells (ICOShighcTfh) are expanded in MG and are associated with the disease severity. Although it is unknown what influences the skew of Tfh in MG, one of the candidates is microRNA (miRNA), especially miR-146a and miR-155, which were reported to be associated with accumulation and function of Tfh. Methods Twenty-four MG patients positive for anti-acetylcholine receptor antibody and 12 HS were enrolled. The expressions of miR-146a and miR-155 in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) were analyzed by a real-time PCR system in association with the cTfh phenotype in MG. To further examine cell-type-specific MIR155HG expression, publicly available single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data from MG patient PBMCs were analyzed. Results The expressions of miR-146a and miR-155 were significantly higher in MG than HS. The level of miR-155 but not miR-146a level showed significant correlation with the frequency of ICOShighcTfh. scRNA-seq analysis revealed that MIR155HG was most highly expressed in a Tfh-like CD4+ T cell cluster characterized by elevated CXCR5, ICOS, PDCD1, and IL21, which was expanded in MG relative to HS (24% vs. 18%), supporting the PBMC-level miRNA findings. miR-155 levels decreased after immunotherapy, paralleling the reduction of ICOShighcTfh in MG. Conclusion Elevated miR-155 expression is associated with pathogenic activation of circulating Tfh cells in MG, supported by single-cell transcriptomic evidence of MIR155HG enrichment in a Tfh-like CD4+ T cell population.

papers.title: Comparative analysis of cytotoxicity, apoptosis, and tumor-progression gene expressions in MCF-7 breast cancer cells treated with Ribociclib, Everolimus, and Doxorubicin: An integrative bioinformatics and experimental study.
papers.authors: Amoei A, Ghotbbahaei M, Barzegar A, Hossein-Nataj H, Lotfi M, Taghiloo S, Asgarian-Omran H.
papers.abstract: Targeted therapy with small-molecule inhibitors (SMIs) is the standard of care for estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer (ER+ BC). While targets for SMIs are known, cellular responses remain unclear. This study compares the effects of the CDK4/6 inhibitor ribociclib (Rib) and the mTOR inhibitor everolimus (Eve) to the anthracycline chemotherapeutic doxorubicin (Dox) in the MCF-7 BC cell line. The expression, prognostic value, and immune infiltration correlates of Programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1), Matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9), Transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) and Vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGF-A) in luminal BC were assessed using UALCAN, KM-Plotter and TIMER2.0. MCF-7 cells were treated with Rib, Eve, and Dox. Half-maximal inhibitory concentrations (IC50) were determined using MTT assay. Apoptosis was analyzed by flow cytometry, and mRNA expression was measured by Real-Time PCR. Target genes were differentially expressed across BC subtypes; high MMP-9 and VEGF-A expression predicted poorer survival; PD-L1, MMP-9, and TGF-β were correlated with immune infiltration. The IC50 values were 11.95 µM, 36.34 µM and 1.396 µM for Rib, Eve, and Dox, respectively. At IC50 concentrations, the percentage of apoptotic cells was significantly higher with Dox. Dox significantly upregulated PD-L1, VEGF-A, and MMP-9. Rib upregulated PD-L1 and induced non-significant increases in VEGF-A and MMP-9, while Eve slightly decreased MMP-9. TGF-β levels remained constant, with increases under Dox and Eve. Cytostatic SMIs preserved a more favorable molecular profile, whereas Dox, despite potent cytotoxicity, paradoxically induced a tumor-progression phenotype in residual cells. Rib-induced PD-L1 overexpression suggests a mechanism of adaptive immune resistance.

papers.title: Integrated transcriptomic analysis and machine learning identify AURKA and CENPM as candidate biomarkers in focal segmental glomerulosclerosis.
papers.authors: Lin X, Huang G, Sun Q, Zhang X.
papers.abstract: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) is a leading cause of steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome and progression to end-stage renal disease, but existing therapeutics and diagnostics are limited. Therefore, reliable diagnostic biomarkers that contribute to FSGS therapy and diagnostics are urgently needed. Gene expression data for FSGS (GSE104948; 37 samples: 16 FSGS vs 21 controls) were obtained from GEO. A weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) was employed. Key genes within significant modules were identified using Support Vector Machine Recursive Feature Elimination (SVM-RFE), random forest (RF), and cytoHubba Maximal Clique Centrality (MCC). Functional enrichment analyses were executed, while diagnostic accuracy was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Immune cell infiltration (ICI) levels were quantified using CIBERSORT, and validation was conducted with an independent external dataset (GSE129973; 20 FSGS vs 20 controls). The green-yellow module demonstrated robust association with the FSGS phenotype, from which 39 candidate genes were selected. Integration of RF, SVM-RFE and cytoHubba analyses pinpointed two primary hub genes: AURKA, which was recovered consistently across cross-validation folds, and CENPM, a less consistently recovered candidate. Functional enrichment underscored the involvement of these genes in pivotal biological processes, particularly mitosis and regulation of the cell cycle. Analysis of immune infiltration revealed significant shifts in the immune microenvironment (IME) of FSGS, correlating elevated expression of AURKA and CENPM with altered ICI patterns. ROC curve analyses showed the diagnostic performance of these genes, with AURKA achieving an AUC of 0.95 and CENPM 0.94 in the training dataset (independent validation: AURKA AUC 0.797, CENPM AUC 0.720). These results showed a consistent direction of change between FSGS patients and healthy controls in an independent validation cohort. Using a combined analytical approach involving WGCNA, machine learning (ML) algorithms, and protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks, this study identified AURKA and CENPM as exploratory tissue-based candidate biomarkers for FSGS, with AURKA being the more robustly supported of the two; both require functional validation and independent confirmation before any therapeutic application can be considered.

papers.title: Recent advances in the molecular pathogenesis of Epstein-Barr virus-associated nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
papers.authors: Kondo S, Dochi H, Komura S, Nakagawa T, Kawasaki H, Hirai N, Kano M, Mizokami H, Matsumura K, Uno D, Ogawa M, Endo K, Misawa K, Kaneda A, Yoshizaki T.
papers.abstract: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) is a major etiologic factor in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). Although persistent latent EBV infection has traditionally been viewed as central to NPC carcinogenesis, recent evidence has broadened our understanding of the dynamic interactions between EBV and host cells. Host genetic and epigenetic alterations may precede EBV infection, establishing a cellular environment permissive for viral persistence. Within this permissive context, latent EBV gene products activate oncogenic signaling, with their effects further reinforced by genomic instability and epigenetic reprogramming. This evolving evidence has also challenged the conventional view that EBV in NPC is predominantly restricted to a latent state. Abortive or partial lytic infection may coexist with latency and contribute to malignant phenotypes, while emerging evidence indicates that productive viral replication can occur in a subset of NPC cells and clinical tumors. In parallel, advances in genomic, epigenomic, single-cell, and spatial technologies have uncovered additional mechanisms, including EBNA1-mediated chromosomal instability, EBV-induced three-dimensional chromatin reorganization, and intricate interactions between EBV-infected tumor cells and the immune microenvironment. Collectively, these findings support a dynamic model in which host susceptibility, evolving EBV infection states, and subsequent genomic, epigenomic, and immune remodeling interact to shape NPC development and progression. This review synthesizes recent advances in the molecular pathogenesis of EBV-associated NPC, with particular emphasis on epigenetic reprogramming and the emerging contribution of EBV lytic infection.

papers.title: What do we really know about human immunometabolism in inflammatory disease?
papers.authors: Gunawardana S, Romero Arocha S, Clarke AJ.
papers.abstract: Cellular metabolism is now recognised as an active regulator of immune cell activation, differentiation, and function. However, much of this conceptual framework derives from in vitro systems and animal models that may not fully reproduce human physiology or disease. Many studies of human immune metabolism are constrained by artificial culture conditions, tissue dissociation, limited pathway coverage, and a reliance on static measurements that do not directly quantify metabolic flux in vivo. Interpretation is further complicated by the use of blood samples as a surrogate for diseases that arise in specialised tissues, such as synovium, gut, and skin, and by the influence of systemic physiology, including hepatic substrate regulation, adipose tissue, endocrine and neuronal signalling, and the gut microbiota. In this review, we examine what current experimental approaches can infer about immune metabolism in humans, with a focus on immune-mediated inflammatory diseases. Oncology provides a valuable methodological precedent through its use of tissue sampling, spatial profiling, and stable isotope tracing, while also illustrating the challenges of assigning metabolic activity to individual cell populations within heterogeneous tissues. We propose five priorities for the field: move beyond blood to inflammatory tissue; complement static abundance with dynamic, stable isotope flux analysis; integrate single cell, spatial, and imaging modalities; incorporate carefully designed human metabolic perturbations; and account for the wider systemic and pre-analytical context. The next phase of human immunometabolism should move from pathway annotation in reductionist models towards dynamic, tissue-resolved, and clinically anchored studies of immune cell metabolism in vivo.

papers.title: Derivation of doxorubicin mutational signatures in cancer.
papers.authors: Skinner KT, Lee BP, Woods CW, Yoon JS, Ho SC, Boot A, Yu W, Rozen SG, Hong AL.
papers.abstract: Doxorubicin is a chemotherapeutic agent used for the treatment of solid and hematopoietic malignancies. Doxorubicin acts as a DNA intercalator and inhibits the topoisomerase II enzyme, leading to double-stranded breaks. We hypothesize that doxorubicin mutagenesis leads to a nonrandom pattern of somatic mutations on the genome, termed a mutational signature. We expose cells to doxorubicin using two different methodologies: (1) continuous exposure of a constant dose of doxorubicin and whole-genome sequencing of single-cell clones (previously published methodology) and (2) pulsed exposure of escalating doses of doxorubicin and whole-genome sequencing of a bulk population. We first confirm that the methodologies do not yield differing results through previously published cisplatin-exposed single-cell clone genome data compared with the dose escalation and bulk genome data. We then derive two doxorubicin signatures. The first, SBS-doxorubicin-1, is defined by an abundance of C > A mutations. The second, SBS-doxorubicin-2, is defined by a higher occurrence of T > C mutations. We then assess for the presence of our signatures within the genomes of patients treated with a doxorubicin-containing regimen. Across 10 bulk immune sorted samples from three patients with follicular lymphoma/diffuse large B cell lymphoma, as well as two metastatic samples from one patient with renal medullary carcinoma, we are able to detect both signatures in 83% of samples, with remaining samples harboring either signature. In summary, we experimentally derive two doxorubicin mutational signatures and demonstrate their presence in patient samples.

papers.title: Multimodal Integration Identifies C16orf74 as an EMT Regulator With Prognostic Relevance in HNSCC.
papers.authors: Huang Z, Anzai T, Lu J, Fukawa Y, Ushio A, Ishimaru N, Podyma-Inoue KA, Watabe T.
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is an aggressive malignancy characterized by marked intratumoral heterogeneity and poor clinical outcomes. Epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) promotes metastasis, immune evasion, and therapeutic resistance. However, the key molecular determinants underlying EMT-associated malignant states remain incompletely defined, and their translation into clinically accessible tools is challenging. In this study, we performed an integrative multiomics analysis to dissect malignant epithelial heterogeneity in HNSCC. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) identified a highly malignant EMT epithelial subpopulation characterized by elevated genomic instability and terminal malignant states. Furthermore, an ensemble of machine learning algorithms prioritized C16orf74 as a key EMT-associated malignant regulator. Spatial transcriptomics localized C16orf74 spatially concentrated at invasive-front and transitory regions associated with distinct tumor microenvironmental niches. Gain- and loss-of-function assays confirmed that C16orf74 regulates EMT activation, migration, invasion, and tumor-sphere formation in HNSCC cells. Mechanistically, integrative regulon, transcriptomic, spatial, and functional analyses identified high-mobility group AT-hook 2 (HMGA2) as a candidate downstream mediator of C16orf74-associated EMT. To translate these biological insights into clinical practice, we developed an EMT-based pathomics prognostic model using hematoxylin and eosin-stained whole-slide images, which achieved robust prognostic stratification. Notably, high-risk group interpretably exhibited a positive correlation with C16orf74 expression, EMT enrichment, an immunosuppressive microenvironment, and resistance to standard chemotherapeutic agents. Collectively, our findings identify C16orf74 as a putative EMT regulator and develop a clinically accessible pathomics model for prognostic and therapeutic stratification in HNSCC.

papers.title: Cellular Proliferation and Reprogramming in Pre-Metastatic Niches: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Vulnerabilities.
papers.authors: Wang S, Song C, Li P, Feng J, Shi X, Lu Q, Duan B, Zhang X, Li S, Luo Y, Fan X, Li Z, Zhang Y, Gu R, Mao W.
papers.abstract: Cancer metastasis, the leading cause of cancer-related mortality, fundamentally depends on the proactive remodelling of distant organ microenvironments by primary tumours through systemic signals, creating a pre-metastatic niche before tumour cell arrival. This review systematically deconstructs the dynamic spatiotemporal evolution of the pre-metastatic niche, highlighting the multi-layered reprogramming of stromal, endothelial and immune cells that collectively cultivate a pro-tumourigenic and immunosuppressive microenvironment. We elucidate the biomechanical and biochemical sensing mechanisms, derived primarily from experimental models, that dictate the fate of disseminated tumour cells, governing the critical balance between dormancy maintenance and proliferative reactivation. Furthermore, we synthesize mechanistic insights alongside human tissue and liquid-biopsy correlative evidence on how metabolic resetting and epigenetic memory may contribute to sustaining pre-metastatic niche stability, and discuss how cutting-edge single-cell and spatial omics technologies are deciphering the intricate multicellular topological architecture of the niche. Ultimately, by mapping these complex systemic interactions across preclinical, biomarker and translational levels, we identify potential therapeutic vulnerabilities and advocate for a paradigm shift toward microenvironment normalization. While clinical validation remains an evolving frontier, targeting pre-metastatic niche priming represents a promising window that warrants rigorous clinical evaluation to intercept nascent metastasis before clinically detectable colonization occurs.

papers.title: Pathogenic mechanisms of Echovirus 18-induced encephalitis in a novel hFcRn transgenic mouse model.
papers.authors: Li F, Huang J, Fu Y, Huang L, Zhang H, Wang Y, Jia L, Xie Z, Chen X.
papers.abstract: Echovirus 18 (E18) poses an escalating neurological threat in children, with its complex pathogenesis impeded by the absence of robust animal models for comprehensive mechanistic investigation. This study establishes an E18-induced viral encephalitis (VE) model in 7-day-old human neonatal Fc receptor (hFcRn) transgenic mice. After intracranial inoculation with 4.0 × 10 6 PFU of E18, mice developed marked signs of infection, characterized by progressive weight loss, motor impairment, elevated viral loads in the brain, and histopathological evidence of VE, ultimately resulting in approximately 75% mortality. The E18-infected mouse brains were accompanied by lymphocytic and granulocytic infiltration, neuronal shrinkage, and focal hemorrhage, with magnetic resonance imaging revealing prominent signal abnormalities in the subarachnoid space and periventricular regions. Interestingly, although all cell types of the brain can serve as carriers of the virus at the single-cell level, E18 exhibits distinct cellular tropism by preferentially targeting astrocytes and microglia rather than neurons and neurofilaments. Additionally, E18 infection orchestrates a complex and adaptive immune response, with dynamic changes among astrocytic subtypes reflecting the evolution of this immune response. Overall, this study successfully establishes a disease model that enhances our understanding of E18-induced encephalitis and provides a valuable platform for evaluating therapeutic interventions and developing vaccines.IMPORTANCEE18 represents an important pathogen in infectious diseases, with potential neurological complications that warrant further investigation. However, due to ethical and technical limitations, its neuropathological mechanisms have long remained unexplored. This study presents a novel encephalitis model using 7-day-old hFcRn Tg mice. The integration of MRI, histopathology, and multi-omics analysis elucidated the molecular mechanisms of viral neural invasion, offering critical insights into pediatric viral encephalitis and potential therapeutic strategies. This animal model provides a valuable platform for understanding E18-induced encephalitis mechanisms and evaluating potential therapeutics and vaccines.

papers.title: Global burden of chewing-tobacco-attributable oral cancer and genomic-transcriptomic profiling of cigarette-smoking-associated oral cavity tumors.
papers.authors: Zheng J, Zhao C, Cheng Y, Liu X, Zhang W, Liu Y, Liu Y, Qiu Y.
papers.abstract: Smokeless chewing tobacco and combustible cigarette smoking are the two primary tobacco-related drivers of lip and oral cavity cancer worldwide, yet global epidemiological registries and public cancer-genomic repositories capture these modalities asymmetrically. We designed a complementary two-component framework to jointly benchmark the macro-epidemiological burden of chewing tobacco and the micro-genomic landscape of cigarette-smoking-associated oral cavity tumors without conflating their distinct exposures. We analyzed the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 dataset to quantify the global and regional burden of lip and oral cavity cancer attributable to chewing tobacco from 1990 to 2021 and projected age-specific burden to 2050. Separately, in a strictly audited cohort of 299 primary oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma (OCSCC) patients from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) with complete clinical covariates and recorded cigarette smoking history (295 with RNA-seq, 292 with whole-exome sequencing, and 288 with both), we performed multivariable differential expression, mutational signature, co-expression network, immune deconvolution, and nested machine-learning analyses. In 2021, chewing tobacco accounted for 37,507 deaths (95% UI 25,312 to 52,128) and 1,131,637 DALYs (95% UI 773,196 to 1,576,992) globally, with 91.7% of deaths concentrated in South Asia and global annual deaths projected to reach 62,840 by 2050 under age-specific demographic decomposition. In the TCGA cigarette-smoking oral cavity cohort, smoking-exposed tumors exhibited higher tumor mutational burden (TMB, p = 1.3 × 10^-7), enrichment of LRP1B and PIK3CA mutations after TMB adjustment (q = 0.027), activation of cytochrome P450 xenobiotic metabolism, and lower expression of an antiviral/interferon-related co-expression module (MEpurple, r = -0.19, p = 9 × 10^-6), whereas TPM-based quanTIseq immune cell fractions did not pass false-discovery-rate correction (FDR > = 0.05). In leak-free nested holdout evaluation (n = 87), a five-feature Random Forest model achieved an AUC of 0.614 (95% CI 0.492 to 0.728) compared with 0.619 for TMB alone. Chewing tobacco imposes a severe, geographically concentrated oral cancer burden centered in South Asia, while cigarette-smoking-associated oral cavity tumors in TCGA display elevated mutational load and altered metabolic-antiviral transcriptional programs without incremental multi-omic classification gain over TMB alone. Because these two components reflect distinct tobacco exposures, the molecular findings in cigarette-smoking tumors do not explain the chewing-tobacco epidemiological burden; rather, they establish a rigorous methodological and molecular reference baseline for future profiling of smokeless-tobacco-associated oral cancer cohorts.

papers.title: Persistent infection is associated with divergent evolution of T cell repertoires.
papers.authors: Chang DY, Bravi B, Malik S, McGuire DJ, Ahmed H, Antia R, Ahmed R, Ghorani E.
papers.abstract: In chronic infection, T cell clones recognizing the same epitope are variably expanded, with some clones evolving to become dominant, while others are lost. Clonal expansion and changes in the repertoire reflect both T cell receptor-intrinsic (TCR-intrinsic) and -extrinsic factors, yet the individuality of TCR repertoires makes it difficult to disentangle how TCR sequence shapes clonal behaviors. To address this, we exploited the observation that TCRs can be grouped into clusters based on sequence similarity. Using complementarity-determining region 3β (CDR3β) sequencing data derived from lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus-specific CD8+ T cells from mice infected early and late in the course of chronic infection, we identified CDR3β clusters ubiquitously shared by all mice. The pattern of CDR3β cluster abundance was highly similar between mice at the early time point in both self-limiting and persistent infection models. Over the course of chronic infection, the pattern of cluster abundance diverged between mice and dominant clones emerged that did not share sequence similarity between mice. This repertoire divergence was not observed in self-limiting infection, where the pattern of cluster abundance established early in infection was stable between mice beyond resolution of infection. In chronic infection, the repertoires of stem-like and exhausted antigen-specific T cells remained similar over time within individual mice, suggesting clonal selection acts on the stem-like pool. Our findings suggest that antigen-specific CD8+ T cell clones expanded early in infection have CDR3β motifs that are shared between mice, supporting a role for TCR structural properties in determining the repertoire structure. Divergent patterns of repertoire composition later in chronic infection suggest that these shared CDR3β motifs are less important in patterning the repertoire than during the initial response and there is greater complexity in factors that sculpt the repertoire over the course of persistent antigen exposure.

papers.title: Single-Cell Map of Early Lung Adenocarcinoma Uncovers Invasion-Associated Tertiary Lymphoid Structures.
papers.authors: Ma P, He C, Cai MC, Wu J, Lu H, Zhou S, Zhang Z, Zhang Q, Chen Y, Zang J, Ye K, Shu Y, Chua CW, Li H, Fan Y, Wang J, Yu Z, Xue X, Zhao X, Zhuang G, Fu Y.
papers.abstract: Early lung adenocarcinoma presenting as ground-glass nodules (GGNs) is increasingly detected in clinical practice. However, robust biomarkers reflecting progression from in situ to invasive disease are incompletely defined. Here, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing, T-cell receptor repertoire profiling, whole-slide immunohistochemistry, multiplex immunohistochemistry, and an orthotopic murine lung adenocarcinoma model to dissect the immune landscape of primary GGNs. We found that these early thoracic lesions harbored abundant infiltrates of innate and adaptive immune cells, but intratumoral T lymphocytes included putative polyclonal bystander clones embedded in an immunosuppressive microenvironment. We further observed a marked stage-dependent increase in T and B cell-rich tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs), dominated by immature configurations, whereas mature TLSs remained relatively infrequent. In mouse allografts, spontaneously arising TLSs were likewise underdeveloped, and LTαβ or LIGHT overexpression, as well as PD-1 blockade, promoted TLS neogenesis and maturation, accompanied by reduced tumor growth. Collectively, our study delineates the immunologic features associated with pathological invasion, identifies a predominance of structurally immature TLS niches, and provides a rationale for further investigating the therapeutic potential of promoting TLS maturation to intercept early lung adenocarcinoma.

papers.title: Genomic, single-cell, and functional profiling of the CD48-CD244 axis and NK cell dysfunction in multiple myeloma.
papers.authors: Patiño-Escobar B, Steinbrunn T, Perez-Lugo L, Rampersaud S, Waller DD, Ordoñez D, Geng H, Salangsang F, Phojanakong P, Camara Serrano JA, Zeng Y, Steri V, Aguilar OA, Mitsiades CS, Wiita AP.
papers.abstract: Multiple myeloma (MM) orchestrates immune evasion by subverting natural killer (NK) cell function. CD48, one of the most abundant NK ligands on MM cells, paradoxically enhances NK cell activation yet is associated with high-risk cytogenetics and poor patient survival. We integrated multiomics (bulk and single-cell RNA-seq, assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing [ATAC-seq], chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing [ChIP-seq]), genome-wide CRISPR knockout/activation screens, and machine learning to dissect CD48 regulation and function. In human MM and Vκ*MYC mouse scRNA-seq datasets, NK cells exhibit stepwise increases in inflammatory and exhaustion signatures and loss of cytotoxic potential as disease progresses. In vitro coculture assays show that CD48 overexpression on MM enhances NK cell cytokine secretion, whereas chronic exposure leads to ex vivo NK dysfunction. In vivo, CD48-overexpressing Vκ*MYC tumors progress more slowly and extend host survival, while NK cell depletion accelerates disease. These findings support a context-dependent role for CD48, potentiating acute NK responses while coexisting with chronic NK exhaustion, and suggest strategies to modulate CD48 for therapeutic benefit.

papers.title: Case Study of a Cross-Platform Evaluation of an Optimized Multicolor Flow Cytometry Immunophenotyping Assay for Human Peripheral Whole Blood.
papers.authors: Mogge L, Gaipl U, Corradini S, Frey B, Donaubauer AJ.
papers.abstract: Flow cytometry is a commonly used single-cell analysis technique that can be applied for the immunophenotyping of human blood samples. Nowadays, increasing numbers of clinical trials include translational research programs utilizing flow-based immune monitoring assays to assess patients' longitudinal immune status. Over time, flow cytometers require regular calibration, quality controls, maintenance, and need to be replaced by new devices after certain years of operation. When flow-based assays are utilized in clinical studies, it is important to transfer and re-establish them thoroughly on new devices to ensure stable measurements. This project describes a detailed and optimized immunophenotyping assay and its transfer from the Gallios flow cytometer to the DxFlex (both from Beckman Coulter). According to the manufacturer, the DxFlex is intended as a successor to the Gallios and features similar lasers and filters. This enables all antibodies and assayed populations to be represented on the new device. However, after calculating the concentrations of cell populations in the blood, deviations were observed between the two devices. It is concluded that calculated absolute values cannot be compared between the two devices, even though the immunophenotyping assay can be successfully measured on the new DxFlex flow cytometer. Switching this specific IPT assay is not feasible in ongoing clinical trials. When transferring a complex assay, parallel comparative measurements are required to ensure reliable data acquisition, population detection, and result comparability.
papers.venue: Cytometry. Part A : the journal of the International Society for Analytical Cytology

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics define a C3-centred multicellular ecology in colorectal liver metastasis.
papers.authors: Ma F, Yu Y.
papers.abstract: Colorectal liver metastasis (CRLM) develops through malignant-cell plasticity and microenvironmental remodeling, yet the spatial principles by which epithelial, stromal, vascular and myeloid states assemble remain poorly defined. We integrated a 136,995-cell single-cell atlas, four spatial transcriptomic sections and bulk-cohort survival analysis. cNMF resolved three recurrent malignant programs-C1 Proliferative-biosynthetic, C2 AP-1 stress-inflammatory and C3 Secretory-invasive immune-like-which recurred across donors (with a rare, patient-associated tuft/chemosensory component in C3) and followed a pseudotime-associated C1-to-C2-to-C3 ordering rather than a demonstrated temporal progression. C3 cells, rare overall and of donor-dependent abundance, showed epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and invasive features, and in exploratory analyses their signature was associated with shorter recurrence-free survival. Continuous RGS1/CTSL programs captured macrophage heterogeneity more robustly than discrete subclusters. Spatial deconvolution revealed recurrent Fib-COL10A1-Endo-GJA5 proximity and variable C3 integration, with focal CTSL-program macrophage interfaces; MAPK and VEGF pathway activity was higher in C3-rich regions, although this association depended on how C3 was measured. An INHBA-CST6-LBH-FSTL3 score, which aggregates C3 and stromal expression, was associated with recurrence in TCGA, with partial external support in GSE39582 and no demonstrated gain over clinical variables. Virtual knockout of CST6 and LBH and LINCS screening prioritized MEK inhibition (PD-0325901) as a candidate for reversing the C3-associated transcriptional state; no target-engagement claim is made. Together, these findings define a spatially variable, C3-centred multicellular ecology in CRLM and provide a testable computational framework nominating recurrence-associated signatures and network-level candidates for experimental validation.

papers.title: The landscape of cell surface target expression in treatment resistant early-stage breast cancer.
papers.authors: Karlsson P, Sharifi MN, Holmberg E, Bakhtiar H, Niméus E, Killander F, Sjöström M, Zhao SG.
papers.abstract: Purpose Disease recurrence after definitive therapy remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality in early-stage breast cancer, with limited options for treatment intensification. Cell surface-targeted (CST) therapies, including antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), radiopharmaceuticals, and immune-based approaches, have demonstrated success in treating malignancies. However, the known CST repertoire in breast cancer is narrow, largely restricted to HER2 and TROP2, highlighting an unmet need for novel targets in treatment-resistant disease. Methods We profiled CST expression using large-scale gene expression datasets annotated with clinical outcomes, including SCAN-B (n ≈ 10,000), aggregated neoadjuvant chemotherapy cohorts (n ≈ 4,000), and the randomized SWEBCG91RT trial (n = 765). CSTs with therapies in clinical trials were prioritized. RNA-protein correlation was assessed using CPTAC and SCMP datasets. Associations with recurrence-free survival (RFS) and treatment response were analyzed using Cox regression and Fisher's exact test with Benjamini-Hochberg correction. Results Of 78 CSTs under active clinical investigation, RNA expression strongly predicted protein expression (median accuracy 80-94%). In ER+ breast cancer treated with endocrine therapy, nine CSTs (including CEACAM5/6, EPCAM, NECTIN4) were associated with significantly worse RFS. Of these, EPCAM and CEACAM5 were also associated with poor outcomes specifically after radiotherapy in the SWEBCG91RT trial. In HER2 + disease, high expression of FOLH1 and TNFRSF10B predicted relapse despite anti-HER2 therapy. In triple-negative breast cancer, six CSTs were associated with residual disease after neoadjuvant therapy. Conclusions These analyses identify potential candidates for repositioning CST drugs, and single-cell analysis revealed substantial intratumoral heterogeneity for several targets, informing payload selection strategies. CSTs associated with treatment resistance across breast cancer subtypes represent actionable opportunities for therapeutic repositioning. These findings provide a framework for rational integration of CST therapies in early-stage breast cancer.

papers.title: Computational modelling of macrophage facilitated cancer metastasis using a cellular Potts model.
papers.authors: Sharma S.
papers.abstract: Breast cancer mortality primarily results from metastatic dissemination. Macrophages are known to actively facilitate cancer cell invasion through the CSF-1/EGF paracrine signalling loop. This signalling loop involves tumour cells secreting colony-stimulating factor 1 (CSF-1) to recruit macrophages, which in turn release the epidermal growth factor (EGF) that promotes tumour cell migration and invasion.
