However, it remains incompletely understood how CSF-1/EGF chemical signalling cues and other related processes like chemotaxis, cell adhesion, and contact inhibition collectively give rise to the coordinated and persistent migration of tumour-macrophage aggregates required for invasion towards the endothelium. Here, a 2D cellular Potts model (CPM) is developed to investigate the spatiotemporal dynamics of how these coupled processes together govern tumour-macrophage aggregate formation and co-migration. Simulations show that metastasis depends on the combined influence of chemoattractant signalling, chemotactic responsiveness, physical cell-cell interactions, and directional migration rather than on any single process alone. In particular, changes in these processes can alter the collective mobility of tumour-macrophage aggregates, resulting in differences in cell displacement and migratory behaviour. Spatial variations in the CSF-1 and EGF fields generate cues for macrophage and cancer cell chemotaxis, with changes in their secretion and degradation rates influencing how these cues develop and persist across the simulation domain. Contact inhibition can attenuate chemotactic migration in dense cellular environments, while directional TAM migration contributes to tumour-macrophage movement towards the endothelium, with metastatic burden maximized at an intermediate directed-motion strength value. Overall, findings herein highlight the non-intuitive effects of changes in individual parameters and provide insight into the conditions that favour coordinated tumour-macrophage migration and invasion towards the endothelium. The framework herein can also help identify additional regulatory mechanisms that can be targeted through chemotherapy or immunotherapy strategies to limit metastasis.

papers.title: Monocyte-macrophage transcriptional features in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma: An exploratory prognostic signature and the potential role of DDX39A.
papers.authors: Cao S, Duan L, Lun S, Gao Z, Wang X, Li Y.
papers.abstract: The immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment contributes to poor outcomes in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). By integrating single-cell transcriptomic data (GSE196756), TCGA data, patient-level pseudobulk analysis, and independent single-cell validation (GSE160269), we identified 315 monocyte-macrophage-associated candidate genes and developed a 10-gene prognostic signature. The signature showed exploratory risk-stratification potential in TCGA and GSE53624 cohorts. Immune infiltration analyses suggested increased myeloid and M2 macrophage-associated signals in high-risk patients. DDX39A knockdown suppressed ESCC cell migration and invasion while increasing apoptosis. Further experiments revealed associations among DDX39A expression, Wnt/β-catenin-related signaling, WISP1 secretion, and macrophage M2-associated phenotypes. Collectively, these findings provide an exploratory molecular framework for investigating ESCC prognosis and suggest a potential role for DDX39A-associated signaling in tumor-macrophage interactions.

papers.title: Antigen-presenting-cell-associated programs in thymoma-associated myasthenia gravis: public transcriptomic reanalysis and archived cell-model observations.
papers.authors: Lu C, Chai Y, Wang Y, Zhang P, Zhang P.
papers.abstract: Thymoma-associated myasthenia gravis (TAMG) involves a complex thymic immune environment, but tissue antigen-presenting-cell (APC) programs do not by themselves establish a soluble-signal mechanism. We re-analyzed public single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data and examined archived records from one Thy0517 AB-thymoma line and a THP-1-derived dendritic cell-like preparation. Donor-resolved single-cell summaries showed antigen-presentation-associated expression across several APC compartments, whereas IL21 transcripts were sparse and most evident in Tfh-like CD4+T cells. IL21R/IL2RG-containing modules were exploratory tissue annotations, not validation of IL-21R signaling in the culture model. In two TAMG sections, unadjusted APC antigen-presentation and maturation/costimulation correlations attenuated after covariate adjustment; associations with migratory DC, Tfh/IL-21 and GC-like B-cell programs differed between sections. A single normal adult thymus sample provided a descriptive, unmatched reference. The retained morphology and CD11c panels document induction of the THP-1-derived preparation, not an effect of subsequent Thy0517 conditioning. A separate cytokine worksheet contained IL-21- and IL-6-labeled entries, but concentration units and calibration could not be verified. Unverified quantitative marker endpoints were removed. Representative CD4+T-cell plots document the assay format only and do not establish frequency or ratio changes. These observations provide descriptive human tissue context and archived cell-model documentation; they do not establish a Thy0517-conditioning effect or an IL-21-specific TAMG mechanism.

papers.title: Interpretable machine learning applied to high-dimensional salivary proteomics in pediatric inflammatory bowel diseases.
papers.authors: Rupp BT, Reyna J, Giunta A, Weaver T, Chason K, Liu J, Gulati AS, Byrd KM.
papers.abstract: Background Inflammatory bowel diseases (IBDs), including Crohn's disease (CD), ulcerative colitis (UC), and inflammatory bowel disease unclassified (IBD-U), are chronic inflammatory disorders of the gastrointestinal tract. Current methods for classification and longitudinal monitoring are invasive, expensive, and often delayed, limiting timely diagnosis and management. This proof-of-concept study reports the first application of high-dimensional salivary proteomics integrated with interpretable artificial intelligence/machine learning (ML) to define a minimal protein signature for pediatric IBD classification with the ultimate goal of informing therapeutic decision-making. Methods Unstimulated saliva from pediatric CD, UC, and IBD-U patients was analyzed using Alamar Biosciences' NULISAseq 250 Protein Inflammation Panel. Logistic regression with recursive feature elimination identified a candidate minimal discriminative signature. Performance was further assessed using follow-up samples. SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) quantified patient-specific protein contributions and assessed biological similarity of IBD-U to CD and UC. Results Differential abundance analysis between UC and CD revealed 53 significantly different proteins. ML identified a 14-protein signature comprising chemokines/cytokines (CCL1, IFNA1-IFNA13, IL12p70, IL34, TNFSF11/RANKL), receptors/ligands (CD40LG, ICOSLG, IL1R2, IL17RA), structural/tissue-remodeling proteins (CD93, GFAP, SPP1), and growth factors/immune modulators (GDF2, GZMA). The proposed model achieved 97.5% balanced accuracy in first-visit pilot samples and 80.2% with matched follow-up samples. SHAP revealed patient-specific drivers and suggested biological alignment of IBD-U cases toward CD- or UC-like profiles. Conclusions This first-in-field integration of salivary proteomics with interpretable artificial intelligence/ML demonstrates that accurate, noninvasive classification of pediatric IBD is possible using minimal biomarker sets. This approach establishes a scalable framework for future longitudinal monitoring and supports earlier and more precise therapeutic interventions.

papers.title: A Transcriptionally Distinct Intermediate Activation State Precedes Langerhans Cell Migration From the Epidermis.
papers.authors: Kiselev A, Schmitter-Sánchez AD, Mishra S, Kim H, Williams S, Park S.
papers.abstract: Langerhans cells (LC) are antigen-presenting cells that form dense epidermal networks for immune surveillance. Upon antigen uptake, LCs are activated and subsequently orchestrate immune responses by migrating into the lymphatic system. However, the regulation of transcriptional programs during activation and the behavior of LCs in vivo during this transition remain poorly understood. Therefore, this study combines single-cell transcriptomic analysis with intravital imaging to reconstruct the activation trajectory of epidermal LCs. In particular, the study generates a high-resolution single-cell transcriptomic dataset comprising over 22 000 high-quality epidermal LCs under both homeostatic and injury conditions. Notably, a distinct intermediate activated state that precedes LC migration was identified and characterized at the level of signaling pathways and transcription factors. The integration of this dataset with external datasets from homeostatic and injured skin reveals wound-specific fibroblasts as the major source of C3, which is the central component of the complement cascade. Moreover, intravital imaging of C3-deficient mice and pegcetacoplan treatment demonstrates that C3 contributes to LC accumulation adjacent to wound sites. Collectively, the study findings identify an activated epidermal LC population and implicate complement signaling in the regulation of LC behavior during skin injury.

papers.title: Tumour-Associated Endothelial Cell Heterogeneity: From Biological Mechanisms to Precision Vascular Targeting.
papers.authors: Zhao K, Wang Z, Xie Y, Zhang Y, Liu S, Xu Y, Cheng H, Huang X, Zhang T, Zhuang L.
papers.abstract: Background Tumour-associated endothelial cells (TECs) are heterogeneous and plastic regulators of the tumour microenvironment. Their angiogenic, metabolic, barrier, and immunoregulatory programs influence tumour perfusion, metastatic dissemination, immune-cell access, and therapeutic response. However, the causal roles and clinical utility of many newly identified endothelial states remain uncertain. Methods This review examines the origins and functional heterogeneity of TECs, drawing on findings from single-cell and spatial studies. It discusses the implications of endothelial states for anti-angiogenic therapy, vascular normalization, immune modulation, drug delivery, combination treatment, and therapeutic resistance. Results Current evidence reveals endothelial states with distinct functional and therapeutic properties, although most remain descriptively characterized and lack causal or clinical validation. We propose a translational framework integrating single-cell and spatial profiling with protein-level validation, functional perturbation, vascular imaging, and longitudinal biomarkers to distinguish endothelial states that warrant suppression, normalization, reprogramming, or selective targeting. Conclusions TEC heterogeneity provides a rationale for precision vascular targeting. Establishing the causal functions and therapeutic relevance of endothelial states will be essential to advance vascular therapy beyond empirical angiogenesis inhibition and guide more selective treatment strategies.

papers.title: Integrated Multi-omics Reveals Molecular Signatures of Rett Syndrome, Informing Future Biomarker Discovery.
papers.authors: Issar JK, Hertzog A, Pang I, Graham ME, Aryamanesh N, Riley LG, Piras IS, Hansen NP, Finney CA, Shvetcov A, Gloss B, Bandodkar S, Dale RC, Sun Q, Ellaway C, Tolun AA, Ho G, Kaufmann WE, Gold WA.
papers.abstract: Rett syndrome (RTT) is a severe neurodevelopmental disorder primarily caused by pathogenic variants in the X-linked methyl-CpG-binding protein 2 (MECP2) gene. Despite numerous clinical trials being conducted, there are limited disease-modifying options available for individuals with RTT. This paucity of effective treatments can in part be attributed to the lack of clinically useful biomarkers that can objectively assess treatment response. Moreover, diagnosis of RTT continues to be clinical, when clinical manifestations are apparent, precluding early therapeutic approaches. Thus, clinical biomarkers of disease stage could improve diagnosis and enable real-time monitoring of response to treatment, providing the earliest possible indications of therapeutic efficacy. Given MeCP2's role as a key regulator of gene transcription, we used an untargeted omics approach to evaluate transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolic profiles in blood from individuals with RTT (n = 9) and age- and sex-matched controls (n = 8). In addition to characterising differential expression at each omic layer, to understand the shared biology and coordinated molecular signals across all omic datasets, we used the unsupervised machine learning framework Multi-Omics Factor Analysis version 2 (MOFA2). The individual omic data consisted of a robust upregulation of genes involved in ribosomal structure and translation together with a downregulation in vesicle trafficking genes. An upregulation in ribosomal machinery and mitochondrial function together with a concomitant downregulation of critical epigenetic regulators, immune-signalling molecules, and cytoskeletal structural anchors was observed in the proteomics, which was supported by the phosphoproteomics. Notably, plasma metabolomics pointed towards alterations in energy substrates and lipid/cholesterol handling, suggesting systemic downstream consequences of primary intracellular disturbances. The integrated MOFA2 data supported the individual omic data revealing a central disease axis principally shaped by the proteome and transcriptome and supported by the metabolome and phosphoproteome, identifying potential biomarkers, including latent biological processes that distinguish RTT from controls (Latent Factor 1) and correlates of clinical severity (Latent Factor 2). Overall, our data reveal a distinctive 'disease state' molecular signature that distinguishes individuals with RTT from controls, where the findings in RTT blood cells are consistent with previously reported altered translational and mitochondrial function and disrupted chromatin regulation, cytoskeletal dynamics, and metabolic signalling. Our integrated multi-omics analyses revealed that PBMC's LTN1, ATRX, CHD8, SPTB, DMTN, PRF1, CD40LG, and PTPRCAP and plasma glutamate are the most promising disease-state (complementary diagnostic) candidate biomarkers while sphingomyelin, RTN3, and MMP1 appear to be the most suitable biomarkers of disease severity. Here, we demonstrate that blood from individuals with RTT reflects the molecular systemic consequences of MeCP2 dysfunction.

papers.title: Spatially integrated transcriptomics maps the metastatic niche in lymph nodes of gastric cancer.
papers.authors: Xie W, Zhang C, Fu X, Fu J, Yang Z, Lin Z, Chen Y, Zhou Y, Lin E.
papers.abstract: Lymph node (LN) metastasis is a major determinant of clinical outcome in gastric cancer (GC), yet the molecular and spatial features of metastatic LN niches remain incompletely defined. Here, we integrated digital spatial profiling (DSP) of primary GC and matched LNs, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), and 10x Genomics Visium spatial transcriptomics. Cross-sectional analysis of cytokeratin-positive regions across primary GC and N1-N3 metastatic lymph nodes (mLNs) identified a hybrid epithelial-mesenchymal expression pattern in N1 samples and prominent immune checkpoint, angiogenic, and receptor tyrosine kinase programs in the N3 group. Deconvolution showed enrichment of exhausted T cells, regulatory T cells, and fibroblasts in mLNs, consistent with immunosuppressive remodeling of the local microenvironment. Cell-cell communication analysis implicated the galectin-9 (LGALS9)-CD45/CD44, CLEC2D-KLRB1, and CCL19/CCL21-CCR7 axes in mLNs. Spatial analysis further revealed compartment-specific heterogeneity, including distinct proliferative, immune, and immunosuppressive programs. Integrating multiple transcriptomic datasets, we derived a 12-gene lymph node metastasis gene signature (LNMGS); high LNMGS scores were associated with poorer overall survival in the TCGA-STAD cohort. Spatial mapping of the LNMGS in primary GC identified an LNMGS-high region displaying a center-to-periphery expression gradient and tending to have a higher inferred copy-number burden. A distance-associated gene signature derived from this gradient was enriched for proliferation, invasion, angiogenesis, immune evasion, and stemness. Together, these findings provide a spatial and molecular framework for lymph node metastasis in GC and highlight potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets for further investigation. © 2026 The Pathological Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

papers.title: Genetically Predicted β-Hydroxybutyrate and Coronary Atherosclerosis: Mendelian Randomization and APOE-Associated Transcriptomic Signatures in Human Atherosclerotic Plaques.
papers.authors: Yang H, Qi W, Liu C, Li Y, Li L, Wu X.
papers.abstract: Aims Ketone bodies are implicated in cardiovascular metabolism, yet the contributions of β-hydroxybutyrate (BHB), acetoacetate and acetone to coronary atherosclerosis remain unclear. Methods We integrated Mendelian randomization (MR), cross-trait GWAS analysis, ApoE pQTL-MR and colocalization to investigate genetic associations with coronary atherosclerosis, complemented by bulk transcriptomic analysis, machine learning-based signature construction, immune infiltration analysis and single-cell analysis to characterize APOE-associated molecular features in human atherosclerotic plaques. Results Genetically predicted BHB was associated with coronary atherosclerosis risk in univariable MR (OR = 1.59, 95% CI: 1.29-1.95, p = 8.8 × 10 -6 ) and remained significant after mutual adjustment for acetoacetate and acetone (OR = 1.58, 95% CI: 1.14-2.18, p = 0.005), whereas neither acetoacetate nor acetone showed a significant association. Cross-trait gene prioritization highlighted APOE for further investigation. ApoE pQTL-MR supported an association between genetically predicted ApoE and coronary atherosclerosis (OR = 1.23, p = 0.003). Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and machine-learning algorithms, including LASSO, random forest, SVM-RFE and XGBoost, identified an APOE-associated five-gene signature comprising XAF1, CEP128, TMEM106A, VEPH1 and ABCB1. The signature achieved an apparent AUC of 0.956 in GSE43292 and AUCs of 0.974 in GSE100927 and 0.736 in GSE28829. High signature scores were associated with immune-inflammatory changes. Single-cell analysis showed enrichment of the signature in macrophages, endothelial cells and fibroblasts, while CellChat analysis identified a macrophage-centred pattern of inferred cell-cell communication. Conclusions These findings identify BHB as the ketone body most strongly associated with coronary atherosclerosis susceptibility and define an APOE-associated multicellular signature in human atherosclerotic plaques with potential value for molecular stratification.

papers.title: Patient-Derived Glioblastoma Organoids for AI-Guided Prediction of Therapeutic Response.
papers.authors: Puja S, Bhavyadharshini A, Geofrey J, Siddharth M, Shubham G, Aliasgar M, Prakash S, Vikas S, Nidhisha S, Akshohini G, Ayushi S, Abhishek C, Sridhar E, Tejpal G, Archya D, Jayant G.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) remains one of the most treatment-refractory brain tumors, with poor survival driven by intratumoral heterogeneity, adaptive therapy resistance, and an immunosuppressive microenvironment that conventional preclinical models have failed to capture. Although these systems offer partial biological insights, none simultaneously preserve patient-specific tumor architecture, microenvironmental complexity, and scalability needed for translational research. Patient-derived GBM organoids address this gap by recapitulating 3D tumor architecture, glioma stem cell (GSC) hierarchies, extracellular matrix (ECM) interactions, and clinically relevant drug response phenotypes in a human-specific system. This review examines GBM organoid biology and engineering, from GSC isolation and ECM scaffold design to maturation, vascular integration, and immune co-culture. We discuss established platforms including NeoCOR and GLICO, and the rationale for incorporating functional vasculature, tumor-immune microenvironment components, blood-brain-barrier (BBB), and blood-cerebrospinal fluid barrier (BCSFB) interfaces. Critically, we propose that integrating artificial-intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) with GBM organoid platforms represents a major opportunity in the field. Convolutional neural networks, ML-based multi-omics integration, drug-genome correlation analysis, and predictive modelling of therapy resistance can transform organoid readouts into clinically actionable decisions. This AI-organoid framework offers a path toward real-time, patient-specific therapy selection, supporting precision-oncology workflows, informing clinical trial design, and reducing GBM therapy failure.

papers.title: Antitumor and Immunomodulatory Effects of Quercitrin Associated with E2F2/ERK/PD-L1 Signaling in Lung Adenocarcinoma.
papers.authors: An Q, Xu J, Shen J, Huang Y, Chen Z, Zhao H.
papers.abstract: Background E2F2 regulates cell-cycle progression and may contribute to tumor immune regulation, but its clinical and biological relevance in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains unclear. Quercitrin has reported anticancer activity, although its molecular effects in LUAD are incompletely understood. Methods E2F2 expression, survival associations, and immune-cell associations were evaluated using TCGA, TIMER2.0, and clinical LUAD specimens. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations assessed the predicted interaction between quercitrin and E2F2. Wound-healing, MTT, immunofluorescence, western blotting, and A549-Jurkat co-culture assays were used to evaluate wound closure, viability, MAPK/ERK signaling, PD-L1 expression, and residual tumor-cell staining. Proteomic and metabolomic analyses characterized exploratory treatment-associated molecular changes. Results E2F2 was upregulated in LUAD and was associated with a non-monotonic pathological stage pattern, poorer unadjusted survival, and estimated infiltration of neutrophils, CD4+ T cells, and CD8+ T cells. Computational modeling predicted a favorable interaction between quercitrin and E2F2 (MM/GBSA binding free energy, -26.45 kcal/mol). Under the tested conditions, quercitrin reduced A549-cell viability, wound closure, E2F2 abundance, ERK phosphorylation, and PD-L1 expression. At the selected 1:1 A549:Jurkat ratio, 150 μM quercitrin reduced residual tumor-cell staining. Exploratory proteomic and metabolomic analyses identified 127 proteins and 213 metabolites with nominally significant abundance differences, respectively. Conclusions Quercitrin-associated changes in LUAD cells coincided with changes in E2F2, ERK phosphorylation, and PD-L1 expression.

papers.title: Metabolic Profiling Combined With Machine Learning for Assessing Clonal Hematopoiesis Status in Chronic Immune Thrombocytopenia: An Exploratory Analysis.
papers.authors: Chen J, Wen Q, Sun T, Liu X, Xue F, Liu W, Fu R, Ju M, Dai X, Chi Y, Wang W, Yang R, Chen Y, Zhang L.
papers.abstract: Clonal hematopoiesis (CH) has emerged as a potential contributor to the pathogenesis of immune thrombocytopenia (ITP), yet the clinical and metabolic features of ITP patients harboring CH-associated mutations remain poorly characterized. We retrospectively analyzed a genomic discovery cohort of 1817 patients with chronic ITP, identifying CH in 196 individuals (10.8%), with DNMT3A as the most frequently mutated gene. In a metabolomic profiling cohort of 539 patients (492 ITP-non-CH, 47 ITP-CH), we characterized plasma metabolic signatures using untargeted LC-MS/MS and systematically evaluated the discriminative capacity of integrated metabolic-clinical features through multiple machine learning algorithms. Differential analysis identified 14 plasma metabolites between ITP-non-CH and ITP-CH patients. The cohort was randomly partitioned into a training set ( n = 377) and an independent test set ( n = 162). Among eight evaluated algorithms, logistic regression with balanced class weighting and 14 metabolites + 3 clinical features (sex, age, PLT) achieved the optimal discriminative balance, with a test AUC of 0.721 (95% CI: 0.57-0.87). Our study reveals distinct hematologic and metabolic dysregulation between ITP-CH and ITP-non-CH, and highlights the potential of integrative hematologic-metabolic signatures for improving disease stratification in ITP.

papers.title: OTUD1 Prevents Immunosuppression via Promoting Lysosomal-Associated Degradation of PD-L1.
papers.authors: Hao Y, Zhou H, Liu Y, Jin M, Feng Q, Li T, Li Q, Zhen Y, Sun T, Li C, Wang D.
papers.abstract: Upregulation of PD-L1 on tumor cells is a pivotal aspect of immune evasion, leading to treatment resistance, tumor recurrence, and metastasis. Understanding the mechanisms that control PD-L1 expression in cancer cells is therefore of paramount importance. In this study, we show that deubiquitinase OTUD1 is downregulated in kidney renal clear cell carcinoma (KIRC), and its low expression is linked to a poor prognosis in patients. Analysis of a public single-cell sequencing dataset revealed that OTUD1 is enriched in specific immune cell populations, indicating its potential for immune modulation. Overexpression of OTUD1 significantly hindered KIRC progression and was associated with decreased PD-L1 expression in both KIRC patients and mouse cancer models. Further investigation uncovered that OTUD1 downregulates PD-L1 abundance and enhances tumor cell sensitivity to cytotoxicity mediated by Jurkat T cells. Mechanistically, OTUD1 interacts with and deubiquitinates the protein kinase AKT, thereby promoting the autophagosome-lysosomal degradation of PD-L1 via the AKT-mTOR-TFEB axis. Moreover, OTUD1 overexpression induced autophagy and enhanced the release or exposure of DAMPs, thereby promoting T cell infiltration into the tumor microenvironment in mice. Our study unveils a novel mechanism by which OTUD1 regulates PD-L1 degradation, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic target in KIRC cancer immunology.

papers.title: A Pan-Hepatic T-Cell Atlas Identifies Disease-Specific Immune Dysfunction and Therapeutic Targets for Immunotherapy.
papers.authors: Chen SY, Wang YY, Zhou SN, Zhou MJ, Li X, Li WZ, Zhu MM, Yang YX, Sun Y, Fan P, Li J, Fan X, Xu R, Jiao YM, Song JW, Zhen C, Shi M, Zhang C, Wang FS.
papers.abstract: Single-cell transcriptomics has greatly advanced insight into hepatic immunity and immunotherapy. However, the absence of an integrated atlas spanning multiple hepatic diseases limits systematic comparisons of immune heterogeneity and dynamics. Here, we established a Pan-HEpatic single-cell Atlas of T cells (Pheat), covering 139 donors, 255 blood and liver samples spanning chronic hepatitis (chronic hepatitis B/C [CHB/CHC], alcohol-associated hepatitis, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis), cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and healthy controls (HC), and delineated profound population-, tissue-, and disease-level heterogeneity of 624,215 T cells, with emphasis on CD8 + exhausted T cells (Tex) and CD4 + regulatory T cells (Treg). Within Tex, intrahepatic precursor Tex (Tex pre ) were depleted in CHB compared with healthy controls and other hepatic diseases. Disease-specific checkpoint dominance (4-1BB in CHB, TIGIT in HCC) in Tex pre was identified and experimentally validated. Panobinostat was predicted and validated to reinvigorate Tex pre in CHB patients. In parallel, effector Treg (eTreg) accumulated in diseased livers and exhibited divergent IL-2-STAT5 signaling-hyperactive in CHB and HCC, suppressed in cirrhosis-indicating distinct immunosuppressive status. Lapatinib/olopatadine enhanced Treg suppressive markers in cirrhosis. Pheat provides a high-resolution atlas of hepatic T cells, revealing disease-specific immune heterogeneity and regulatory programs that inform cellular and molecular targets for potential immunotherapy.

papers.title: A Novel Perspective on the Pathogenesis of Arthritis From the PANoptosis Framework: From Cell Death Networks to Macrophage Immune Infiltration.
papers.authors: Song C, Li F, Luo Y, He Y, Zhou Y, Liu Y, Fu Z, Liu Z.
papers.abstract: Arthritis, particularly rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and osteoarthritis (OA), comprises a group of complex disorders characterized by chronic inflammation and progressive joint structural destruction. RA represents an autoimmune condition with robust synovial inflammation, whereas OA manifests mainly as low-grade degenerative inflammation. In recent years, the role of programmed cell death (PCD) in the pathogenesis of arthritis has attracted increasing attention; mechanistic evidence for PANoptosis is more abundant in RA, while its contribution in OA remains putative. However, traditional investigations focusing on single cell death pathways are insufficient to account for the persistence of inflammation and the complexity of cell fate decisions observed in arthritic conditions. PANoptosis, a recently defined integrated mode of cell death, is orchestrated by the PANoptosome complex, which coordinates apoptosis, necroptosis and pyroptosis. This conceptual framework provides a novel perspective for understanding the multidimensional pathological mechanisms underlying arthritis. In this review, we systematically delineate the core concepts and molecular basis of PANoptosis, and explore its crosstalk with necroptosis, pyroptosis, apoptosis, ferroptosis and autophagy within the arthritic microenvironment. Particular emphasis is placed on the pivotal role of macrophages as central executors of PANoptosis in mediating immune cell infiltration and amplifying inflammatory responses. Furthermore, we discuss emerging therapeutic strategies targeting PANoptosis-related pathways. By integrating the 'PANoptosis-immune infiltration-inflammatory feedback' axis, this work aims to provide a novel theoretical framework for elucidating disease mechanisms and advancing clinical interventions in arthritis. Furthermore, we summarize candidate PANoptosis-related biomarkers and discuss existing translational bottlenecks for their clinical deployment.

papers.title: The impact of TLRs/NLRs signaling pathway-mediated CXCL8 regulation on macrophage polarization in oral squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.authors: Li P, Sun H, Sun J, Hu X.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to elucidate the regulatory mechanism underlying the TLRs/NLRs/CXCL8 signaling axis in macrophage polarization and its impact on the malignant phenotypes of oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), using an integrated in vitro and in vivo experimental design. We established CXCL8 knockdown (si-CXCL8) and overexpression (pc-CXCL8) models in THP-1 human monocytic cells. Following confirmation of transfection efficiency, the subcellular localization and expression levels of CXCL8 were analyzed in phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA)-differentiated macrophages. The selective NLRP3 inhibitor INF39 was administered in combination with si-CXCL8 or pc-CXCL8 to investigate the crosstalk between the TLRs/NLRs pathway and CXCL8, as well as their combined effects on macrophage polarization. Finally, differentially treated macrophages were co-cultured with HSC-3 OSCC cells to evaluate changes in tumor cell proliferation, migration, invasion, apoptosis, stemness, inflammation, and oxidative stress; in vivo, HSC-3 cells preconditioned by co-culture with differentially treated macrophages were subcutaneously injected into nude mice to establish a xenograft model, and tumor growth together with relevant molecular markers was assessed. Bioinformatics analysis identified CXCL8 as the core hub gene common to both macrophages and OSCC, with the TLRs/NLRs pathway being the most significantly enriched signaling cascade. Protein-protein interaction analysis predicted functional associations between CXCL8 and TLR1, TLR4, MyD88, and NLRP3. INF39 treatment downregulated the protein expression of both TLRs/NLRs pathway components and CXCL8, and promoted macrophage polarization toward the M2 phenotype. CXCL8 knockdown further enhanced INF39-induced M2 polarization, whereas CXCL8 overexpression largely reversed this effect. Functionally, M2 macrophages driven by INF39-mediated suppression of the TLRs/NLRs/CXCL8 axis significantly enhanced HSC-3 cell proliferation, migration, invasion, stemness, and oxidative stress, while suppressing apoptosis. Consistent with the in vitro findings, in vivo xenograft experiments showed that INF39 promoted tumor growth, whereas CXCL8 overexpression reversed this effect, indicating that this axis regulates OSCC progression via remodeling of the tumor immune microenvironment. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that the TLRs/NLRs/CXCL8 axis modulates macrophage polarization to control the malignant behavior of OSCC cells in vitro and in vivo, providing a mechanistic basis for the development of novel immune-targeted therapies for OSCC.

papers.title: Construction of a UBE2S- and Ferroptosis-Based Prognostic Model for Hepatocellular Carcinoma and Validation of UBE2S-Mediated Ferroptosis.
papers.authors: Zhang H, Yao J, Cao J, Guo Z, Jiang W, Li K, Wang X, Mo Z.
papers.abstract: Purpose This study is aimed at exploring whether ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme E2 S (UBE2S) influences hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) progression through ferroptosis and at constructing a UBE2S-related ferroptosis prognostic model (UFP) for predicting clinical outcomes in HCC patients. Methods Bioinformatics approaches were employed to examine how UBE2S expression relates to both HCC prognosis and ferroptosis. Tumor immune infiltration was assessed using CIBERSORT with the LM22 signature matrix. The prognostic accuracy of the UFP, which integrates CENPA and PAGE1, was assessed via survival analysis, ROC curves, and calibration plots. For experimental validation, ferroptosis-related markers were measured following UBE2S overexpression or knockdown, or after treatment with the ferroptosis inducers erastin and sorafenib. Additionally, tumor weight, size, and ferroptosis-associated proteins were examined in a xenograft model following combined UBE2S knockdown and sorafenib treatment. Results In HCC, elevated UBE2S expression predicted poor prognosis, suppressed ferroptosis, and correlated with an immunosuppressive microenvironment. The UFP model demonstrated robust prognostic performance, as validated using ICGC and single-cell datasets. UBE2S knockdown promoted ferroptosis, as shown by increased Fe 2+ , MDA, and ROS levels and decreased GSH, whereas UBE2S overexpression reversed erastin-induced ferroptosis. Moreover, UBE2S knockdown downregulated GPX4 and SLC7A11, whereas UBE2S overexpression upregulated these proteins. Sorafenib reduced UBE2S levels, and UBE2S overexpression reversed sorafenib-induced ferroptosis. In xenograft models, UBE2S knockdown combined with sorafenib reduced tumor growth and enhanced ferroptosis. Conclusion The UFP model serves as a novel prognostic biomarker for HCC outcomes. Mechanistically, UBE2S suppression promotes ferroptosis and inhibits tumor progression, highlighting this protein as a promising therapeutic candidate. Collectively, our results offer fresh perspectives on HCC management strategies.

papers.title: Baseline TCR clonality predicts reproducibility of CD4+ clonotypic expansions in antigen-stimulated TCR sequencing-based assays, without consistent evidence of a CD4-selective effect of cryopreservation.
papers.authors: Li S, Schuele C, Henry C, Singh D, Steinberg O, Dykema A, Presson B, Zhang L, Zeng Z, Ji H, Smith KN.
papers.abstract: An increasing number of T cell assays use antigen-driven clonotypic expansions as a functional readout. Prior work has suggested that cryopreservation can negatively impact CD4+ T cell function, however its impact on T cell receptor (TCR) sequencing-based assays has not been examined. Reliable identification of antigen-specific responses requires a highly reproducible antigen-agnostic background repertoire, as measured by strong clonal overlap between technical replicates. In this study, we systematically compared the effects of varying cryopreservation time on the reproducibility of CD4+ and CD8+ clonotypic expansions. CD4+ overlap was lower than CD8+ overlap in three of four donors, although the magnitude varied among donors. In the fourth donor, CD4+ and CD8+ overlap were similar when fresh and CD4+ exceeded CD8+ overlap after cryopreservation. Interestingly, the intrinsically lower baseline clonality of the CD4+ T cell repertoire was strongly associated with lower reproducibility of subsequent clonotypic expansions. This study therefore supports baseline TCR clonality as a predictor of clonotypic expansion reproducibility and shows that cryopreservation was associated with reduced repertoire overlap overall, but there was no consistent evidence that this effect differed between CD4+ and CD8+ assays. These findings have important implications for experimental design and data interpretation of TCR sequencing-based functional T cell studies and suggest pre-assay clonality screening as a testable strategy, warranting prospective validation, for studies using CD4+ clonotypic expansions as the primary endpoint.

papers.title: Identification and immune response of CD8α⁺ T cells in grouper (Epinephelus fuscoguttatus × E. lanceolatus) after vaccination at the early stage.
papers.authors: Liu Y, Jiang X, Tang X, Sheng X, Chi H, Cui C, Xing J, Zhan W.
papers.abstract: CD8⁺ T cells are key mediators of cellular immunity, their dynamics varied by vaccination stage. In this study, anti-CD8α polyclonal antibodies (Abs) were produced and CD8α⁺ T cells were characterized. Then groupers were vaccinated with inactivated nervous necrosis virus, the proportions of CD8α+ T cells, and expression of cd8α in head kidney were analyzed using flow cytometry and single-cell RNA sequencing, respectively. The results showed that anti-CD8α Abs could recognize the recombinant CD8α at 36.4 kDa, be co-localized with ZAP-70. At 3rd day post immunization, the proportion of CD8α⁺ T cells increased markedly to 12.52 ± 0.81%. Four subsets of CD8α⁺ T cells (sub-cluster 0 as naïve CD8α⁺ T cells, sub-cluster 1 as innate-like CD8α⁺ T cells, sub-cluster 2 as cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs) 1, and sub-cluster 3 as CTLs2) were identified. Naïve CD8α⁺ T cells highly expressed T cell surface marker tcr and cd3, which might be the starting point of CD8 T cell differentiation; innate-like CD8α⁺ T cells showed high expression of cd74, cd83, and mhc-Ⅱ, and the differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were enriched in lysosome and phagosome pathway, the percentage of this subset rose by 6.6% compared to the PBS group (10.1%); CTLs1 exhibited expression of prf1 and gzmb; Besides prf1, CTLs2 expressed the non-specific cytotoxic cell receptor protein-1, the DEGs were enriched in the natural killer cell-mediated cytotoxicity pathway, its proportion increased to 9.8% after vaccination. These data indicated that CD8α⁺ T cells were activated at the early immunization stage, and presented crosstalk of innate cellular immunity and dual cytotoxic activities. This study elucidated CD8α⁺ T cell profiles and immune responses, offering insights into vaccine protective mechanisms in teleosts.

papers.title: CD97 Modulates M1-Like Macrophage Activation and Function to Influence the Immune Microenvironment and Tumor Progression in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer.
papers.authors: Peng P, Zhou P, Liu Z, Shen H, Hu C, Jiang J.
papers.abstract: Background CD97 is overexpressed in various cancers, but its function and immunoregulatory role in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the expression, function, and potential regulatory mechanisms of CD97 in TNBC. Methods CD97 expression, clinical associations, and immune infiltration were evaluated using TCGA, KM Plotter, and GEO bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomic datasets. THP-1-derived M1a/M1b macrophage models with CD97 knockdown or overexpression were used to assess phagocytosis, cytokine secretion, and effects on tumor and endothelial cells. Zinc modulation, NF-κB inhibition, Western blotting, pseudotime analysis, transcription-factor screening, and network analyses were used to explore potential mechanisms. Results CD97 was upregulated in TNBC and enriched in M1 macrophages. In a pooled KM Plotter analysis, high CD97 expression was associated with favorable relapse-free survival; however, CD97 was not significantly associated with overall survival in the TCGA-TNBC cohort in univariable or stage-adjusted Firth Cox analyses. In M1a macrophages, CD97 perturbation altered phagocytic activity, tumor-cell apoptosis, intracellular zinc homeostasis, and NF-κB signaling, with pharmacological inhibition supporting NF-κB as a downstream mediator. In M1b macrophages, CD97 knockdown increased, whereas overexpression decreased, MDA-MB-231 migration and invasion in vitro. SPI1 perturbation altered CD97 expression, supporting SPI1 as a potential upstream regulator rather than establishing direct transcriptional control. Conclusion CD97 is associated with immune-active features in TNBC and modulates macrophage functions in vitro. Its prognostic relevance appears context- and dataset-dependent, and further in vivo and clinical validation is required before translational application.

papers.title: [Preliminary study on immune infiltration characteristics and prognostic value of the ferroptosis suppressor CAV1 in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma].
papers.authors: Liu GL, Zhang H, Wang R, Yang FR, Sun HK, Shi RX, Yang F.
papers.abstract: Objective: To identify key ferroptosis suppressor genes in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), and to comprehensively analyze their expression patterns, prognostic value, immune infiltration characteristics, and preliminary biological functions. Methods: Ferroptosis suppressor genes were obtained from the FerrDb database, and the HNSCC cohort from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) was used to evaluate their expression profiles. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis was performed to determine the prognostic value of ferroptosis suppressor genes. Immune infiltration analysis, immune checkpoint correlation analysis, and the Tumor Immune Dysfunction and Exclusion (TIDE) algorithm were used to assess the immune microenvironment and predicted response to immunotherapy. In addition, GSE181919 single-cell data, immunohistochemistry, Western blotting, and in vitro functional experiments were used to preliminarily validate the cellular source, expression, and biological role of CAV1. Results: Forty-eight ferroptosis suppressor genes were retrieved from FerrDb, and 10 differentially expressed genes were identified in the TCGA HNSCC cohort. Among them, CAV1 was significantly upregulated. High CAV1 expression was associated with poorer overall survival and disease-specific survival in patients with HNSCC ( P =0.009 and P =0.021, respectively). Immune analysis showed that high CAV1 expression was associated with reduced CD8+T-cell infiltration, increased expression of immune checkpoint-related genes, and a poorer predicted response to immunotherapy. External validation using the GSE25099 dataset further confirmed that CAV1 expression was significantly higher in oral squamous cell carcinoma tissues than in normal tissues ( P P P Conclusions: CAV1 may serve as a potential prognostic biomarker in HNSCC and is associated with an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Preliminary experimental findings further support a tumor-promoting role of CAV1 in oral squamous cell carcinoma, whereas the causal mechanisms linking CAV1 to immune infiltration and ferroptosis resistance require further validation.

papers.title: Unraveling the Diabetes-Inflammation Axis with Single-Cell Analysis and Two-Decade Bibliometric Mapping.
papers.authors: Li J, Luo Y, Ma J, Li S, Sun M.
papers.abstract: Background Diabetes is a multifactorial chronic metabolic disorder in which chronic low-grade inflammation contributes to the initiation and progression of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Investigations of the diabetes-inflammation axis have remained persistently compartmentalized, compelling a systematic synthesis of macroscale bibliometric trajectories with microscale microenvironmental circuitry. Purpose This study integrates a 20-year bibliometric analysis with single-cell transcriptomic analysis to characterize the research landscape and examine inflammatory activity at cellular resolution. Methods A corpus of 55,147 English‑language publications spanning 2006-2026 was curated from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC). CiteSpace, Bibliometrix, and Tableau were harnessed to perform collaboration network mapping, co‑citation dissection, and thematic evolution tracing. In parallel, single-cell RNA sequencing data from two T2DM and two control peripheral blood mononuclear cell samples (GSE280401) were analyzed; after quality control, 2,611 T2DM cells and 4,138 control cells were retained, AUCell was used to quantify inflammatory pathway activity, and CellChat was used to infer intercellular immune communication. Results Macroscopically, the field has witnessed exponential publication acceleration, with China and the United States constituting the dominant research poles and U.S. institutions commanding disproportionate network centrality. The thematic epicenter has undergone a decisive migration from classical inflammatory cytokine postulates toward immunometabolic network orchestration and multi‑target therapeutic frameworks, while cardiovascular protection, oxidative stress, and molecular docking have crystallized as the defining frontier. At the single-cell level, T cells were the most abundant population, overall inflammatory-response scores were higher in T2DM cells, and CellChat suggested reduced global communication with relative enrichment of several pro-inflammatory pathways. Conclusion By erecting a macro-micro dual‑scale knowledge architecture, this study renders visible the foundational intellectual scaffolding and evolutionary trajectory of the diabetes-inflammation axis. The findings identify testable priorities in immunometabolic regulation and ligand-receptor signaling that require confirmation in larger cohorts and functional studies.

papers.title: Integrated Machine Learning and Experimental Validation Identify Shared Aging-Related Molecular Signatures in Alzheimer's Disease and Osteoporosis.
papers.authors: Guo X, Guo Z, Peng T, Pan J, Zhang M, Ye X, Wen J, Liu X, Li Y, Lin X.
papers.abstract: Background Aging is a key biological driver implicated in the initiation and progression of both Alzheimer's Disease (AD) and Osteoporosis (OP). However, the shared aging-related molecular alterations underlying these disorders remain incompletely understood. Methods Transcriptomic datasets of AD and OP, together with curated aging-related genes (ARGs), were systematically collected. Differential expression analysis was conducted using the limma algorithm, followed by weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) to identify disease-associated gene modules. Multiple machine learning algorithms were subsequently employed to prioritize candidate biomarkers, and model interpretability was assessed using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Immune infiltration profiles were characterized via CIBERSORT and single-sample gene set enrichment analysis (ssGSEA). Finally, quantitative real-time PCR (RT-qPCR) was conducted to validate the expression of six core candidate genes. Results Integrated analysis identified 228 aging-related genes shared by AD and OP. EGR1, NFKBIA, UQCRC2, RB1, CREBBP, and NDUFV1 were selected based on the comparative performance of 130 machine learning models for disease prediction. Enrichment analyses linked these genes to cellular senescence, inflammatory signaling, mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation, and cell-cycle regulation, suggesting convergent aging-related alterations in AD and OP. RT-qPCR analysis in the D-galactose-induced senescence models revealed cell-type-specific expression patterns: all six genes were significantly altered in HT22 cells, whereas EGR1, NFKBIA, UQCRC2, and NDUFV1 were significantly altered in MC3T3-E1 cells, with no significant changes observed in RB1 or CREBBP. Moreover, they exhibited robust diagnostic potential, as reflected by nomogram analyses, and showed significant correlations with immune cell infiltration profiles. Conclusion This study elucidates shared aging-related genes linking AD and OP. The six identified hub ARGs demonstrate significant immunological relevance and diagnostic value. Collectively, these findings offer novel insights into shared pathogenic mechanisms and highlight potential targets for integrated therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Urolithin A ameliorates experimental autoimmune myasthenia gravisin association with mitochondrial quality control-related and inflammasome signaling changes.
papers.authors: Zhang N, Kong X, Yu S, Peng S, Xin G, Xu F, Geng Y, Zhu G, Zhang H, Wang L.
papers.abstract: Objective To characterize peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) remodeling in myasthenia gravis (MG) at the pathway and transcriptomic level, and to evaluate whether urolithin A (UA) ameliorates experimental autoimmune myasthenia gravis (EAMG) in association with altered mitochondrial quality control-related and NLRP3 inflammasome signaling. Methods Single-cell RNA-sequencing data from two patients with stable MG and two with MC were analyzed. After quality control, 8414 stable-MG cells and 19,333 MC cells were retained. Cell composition, pathway scores, pseudobulk differential expression, gene-set enrichment, and ligand-receptor interactions were assessed. In parallel, EAMG rats were assigned to control, EAMG, EAMG+UA, or EAMG+UA + chloroquine groups (n = 6/group). Clinical, serological, inflammatory, ultrastructural, mitochondrial quality control-related, and inflammasome-related outcomes were evaluated. Results MC samples showed heterogeneous immune remodeling, including monocyte enrichment in one patient. Across immune-cell subsets, MC was associated with increased inflammatory, inflammasome/pyroptosis, oxidative-stress, chemotaxis, and lysosome-autophagy programs, whereas mitochondrial quality control-related changes were weaker and cell-type dependent. Exploratory analysis suggested enhanced TNFSF13B-TNFRSF13C interaction scores toward B-cell subsets. In EAMG rats, UA reduced clinical weakness, anti-acetylcholine receptor antibodies, and pro-inflammatory cytokines; improved splenic mitochondrial ultrastructure and PINK1/Parkin-associated mitochondrial quality control marker profiles; and suppressed NLRP3/caspase-1/GSDMD-N signaling. Chloroquine partially reversed these effects. Conclusion Exploratory scRNA-seq analysis of four patients suggests that MC is associated with pathway-level enrichment of inflammasome/pyroptosis and autophagy/lysosome programs, whereas mitochondrial quality control-related signals were weaker and cell-type-dependent. The EAMG findings support an association between UA treatment, improved mitochondrial quality control-related marker profiles, and reduced inflammasome activation.

papers.title: Molecular mechanisms of colorectal cancer: from carcinogenesis and molecular classification to targeted therapy.
papers.authors: Aldeyarbi S, Elhanafy E, Saber-Ayad M, Abu Almaaty AH, Sagheer A, Hassan MK.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a heterogeneous disease that results from the progressive accumulation and interactions at multiple levels of genetic alterations, which lead to the transformation of normal colonic epithelium into malignant colorectal tumors. Understanding the molecular basis of CRC pathogenesis, together with the interactions between genetic alterations, epigenetic modifications, environmental and lifestyle factors, is essential for improving prevention, diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment strategies. This review aims to provide a critical reference point for understanding the temporal dynamics of colorectal carcinogenesis, the evolution of molecular classification systems, including their computational and machine-learning foundations and emerging image-based prediction approaches, molecular drivers and the tumor microenvironment (TME) of CRC by summarizing the most investigated molecular pathways involved in CRC pathogenesis and their role as biomarkers for early CRC diagnosis based on the three main molecular mechanisms of colorectal carcinogenesis: chromosomal instability (CIN), microsatellite instability (MSI), and CpG island methylator phenotype (CIMP). Importantly, emerging evidence reveals that the TME acts as an important factor in driving CRC progression by regulating the immune system through dynamic cellular and molecular interactions. In particular, tumor metabolic reprogramming and microbiota-driven alterations act as major drivers of therapy resistance and immune escape. Combining these mechanisms will enhance biomarker discovery and aid in developing precision medicine for patients with CRC. This review also highlights the regulatory roles of key signaling pathways, including Wnt/β-catenin, epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), tumor protein p53 (TP53), and transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) signaling, during CRC initiation and progression, while further addressing current targeted therapies and emerging precision-based and experimental therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Gold Nanorod-Based USP8 Inhibition Combined with Photothermal Therapy Enhances Antitumor Efficacy in Gastric Cancer.
papers.authors: Zheng Q, Wang H, Huang J.
papers.abstract: Background Gastric cancer (GC) remains a major global malignancy with limited therapeutic options for advanced disease. Ubiquitin-specific peptidase 8 (USP8) is a deubiquitinating enzyme involved in tumor progression and immune regulation, but its therapeutic potential in GC remains incompletely explored. Methods Public multi-omics data, including The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), The Cancer Dependency Map (DepMap), single-cell transcriptomic, spatial transcriptomic, and immune-infiltration analyses, were used to investigate the biological relevance of USP8 in GC. A gold nanorod (GNR)-based nanoplatform coated with silicon dioxide (SiO₂) and loaded with the USP8 inhibitor DUB-IN-2 was constructed and designated GNR@SiO 2 -USP8i. The physicochemical properties, drug loading, release behavior, photothermal performance, cellular uptake, cytotoxicity, reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) damage, and in vivo antitumor efficacy were evaluated. Results USP8 was upregulated in GC and preferentially enriched in malignant cells. DepMap and experimental validation showed that USP8 contributed to GC cell proliferation. Immune analyses suggested that high USP8 expression was associated with reduced CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration and altered C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 12 (CXCL12)-C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 4 (CXCR4) signaling. Further experiments showed that USP8 manipulation was accompanied by concordant changes in protein kinase B (AKT) phosphorylation and CXCL12 expression and influenced Jurkat cell chemotaxis. GNR@SiO 2 -USP8i exhibited effective DUB-IN-2 loading, near-infrared (NIR)-responsive release, and favorable photothermal performance. Upon NIR irradiation, GNR@SiO 2 -USP8i markedly reduced GC cell viability, increased ROS generation and DNA damage, and suppressed tumor growth in vivo. Conclusion GNR@SiO 2 -USP8i integrates USP8 inhibition with NIR-triggered photothermal therapy and demonstrates enhanced antitumor activity in GC, supporting further investigation of USP8-targeted nanotherapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Profiling of the T Cell Receptor Repertoire Reveals Different Immunological Signatures Between Mild and Severe H1N1 Infection.
papers.authors: Yang J, Zhao X, Xiao D, Zhang H, Lu H.
papers.abstract: Severe H1N1 influenza remains a global health concern, but the immunological mechanisms underlying disease severity are not fully understood. In this study, we used high-throughput sequencing to profile the T cell receptor beta chain (TRB) complementarity-determining region 3 (CDR3) repertoire in 24 H1N1 patients (12 mild, 12 severe) during the 2009 pandemic. Our analysis revealed significant differences in TRB diversity and clonal expansion between severity groups. Severe patients had significantly reduced TRBV11-3 usage and overall TRB diversity, as indicated by lower Shannon entropy and fewer clonotypes. Twelve TRBV-BJ combinations were downregulated, whereas one was upregulated in severe cases. Similarly, 20 V-D-J combinations were significantly less frequent, and two were more prevalent in severe patients. Severe infection was associated with a higher proportion of hyper-expanded clones, indicating an intense oligoclonal T cell response that narrows repertoire diversity. These characteristic CDR3 repertoire changes provide important insights into the immunopathogenesis of severe influenza and may inform the development of new diagnostic approaches and T cell-targeted therapies. Our findings highlight the value of TCR repertoire profiling for stratifying disease severity and guiding future research on emerging influenza viruses, with potential for translating immunological insights into clinical applications.

papers.title: Decoding neutrophil spatial heterogeneity and clinical implications in breast cancer.
papers.authors: Xu YZ, Wu XR, Qiu ZY, Li YW, Dai LJ, Su GH, Zhang H, Zhang HY, Li M, Lv H, Xiao Y, Zhao S, Shen M, Jiang YZ, Ma D, Shao ZM.
papers.abstract: Neutrophils are heterogeneous and critical components of the tumor microenvironment, yet their spatial heterogeneity and clinical implications remain poorly understood. We establish large-scale breast cancer cohorts integrating AI-powered computational pathology (n = 1,113) and single-cell spatial omics (n = 104) to investigate the clinical relevance and biological mechanisms underlying neutrophil spatial patterns. Clinical implications were greatest in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC): neutrophil-tumor cell proximity associated with favorable prognosis, while neutrophil-immune cell proximity predicted superior immunotherapy response. Combining these patterns with established biomarkers improved TNBC stratification for prognosis and immunotherapy efficacy. Spatial omics and experimental validation demonstrated that tumor-proximal neutrophils enhanced MHC I expression on tumor cells via inflammatory crosstalk, promoting immune-mediated tumor clearance and improved prognosis. Neutrophils adjacent to immune cells exhibited an antigen-presenting phenotype, augmentable by targeting polyamine metabolism. Our study highlights the functional diversity and spatial heterogeneity of neutrophils and provides a translational strategy with routine computational pathology.

papers.title: Immunophenotypic Profiles of General Chinese Population during Natural Aging.
papers.authors: Li Y, Wang B, Han X, Dang J, Qiu JG, Liu B, Wang W, Zhou F, Zhao Y, Zhang X, Hao L, Ding L, Chen X, Zhou Q, Su W, Jiang B, Qian F, Ding X.
papers.abstract: Understanding the interplay between the immune system's dynamics and the natural aging process is crucial for developing potential strategies to mitigate age-related health challenges. Here, we investigated how immunophenotypic profiles vary with the natural aging process, daily practices, and physiological characteristics within a general population of 605 healthy individuals from the Central China Cohort. Utilizing mass cytometry on peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) samples, we acquired over 57 million single-cell data in total from this cohort. These cells were clustered into 50 distinct immune cell subsets. Additionally, we gathered detailed questionnaires from every participant with 764 questions concerning their physical and physiological metrics, lifestyles, and socioeconomic status. By leveraging bootstrap lasso and logit regression models, we endeavored to forecast age and gender based on immunophenotypic profiles. Our investigations unveiled significant correlations between chronological age and specific immune cell clusters such as CD27+CD28+ naïve T and γδ T cells and CD38+ pDCs, showcasing discernible age-related patterns. Furthermore, we established immune ages through the regression models and calculated the age differentials relative to the chronological age, which shed light on the relationships between younger or older immune ages and various body metrics and lifestyles. By offering a comprehensive overview of immune cell profiles in a sizable healthy cohort through mass cytometry, this data resource advances our comprehension of the roles played by immune systems and lifestyles in the aging process.

papers.title: LSEC-derived CXCL9 orchestrates immune recruitment and hepatocyte reprogramming in liver fibrosis.
papers.authors: Li J, Di Q, Zhou X, Chang M, Chen W.
papers.abstract: Chronic liver injury involves complex intercellular communication, yet the contribution of non-classical immune cell populations remains incompletely understood. Here, we identify liver sinusoidal endothelial cell (LSEC)-derived CXCL9 as a pivotal regulator of hepatocyte reprogramming and fibrogenesis in chronic liver injury. Through the integration of bulk transcriptomic profiling, single-cell RNA sequencing, and in vitro hepatocyte assays, we demonstrate that CXCL9 is robustly upregulated in LSECs, rather than Kupffer cells or hepatic stellate cells, following toxic liver injury. KEGG enrichment analysis reveals significant activation of the chemokine signaling pathway (NES = 1.75, P .adj = 1.9 × 10 -4 ), and functional experiments show that exogenous CXCL9 potently induces both regenerative gene ( Hbegf) and pro-inflammatory gene expressions ( Ccl2 , Cxcl2 , Il6 , and Tnf ) in primary hepatocytes ( P < 0.0001-0.01). Gain- and loss-of-function co-culture models further confirm that LSEC-derived CXCL9 is both necessary and sufficient for hepatocyte inflammatory activation and regenerative responses, predominantly via CXCR3 signaling. These findings reveal an underappreciated LSEC-CXCL9-CXCR3 axis as a driver of maladaptive parenchymal reprogramming and fibrogenesis, expanding the paradigm of hepatic chemokine biology and highlighting a novel therapeutic target for chronic liver disease.

papers.title: Neutrophils are known by their neighbors in breast cancer.
papers.authors: Pei S, Ng LG.
papers.abstract: In this issue of Cancer Cell, Xu et al. combine large-scale computational pathology, spatial omics, and functional experiments to examine neutrophil organization in triple-negative breast tumors. They identify two neutrophil niches with different clinical associations: tumor-proximal neutrophils are linked to favorable prognosis, whereas neutrophils near immune cells associate with immunotherapy response.

papers.title: Probing Molecular Binding Mechanisms between a Therapeutic Antibody and an Antigen Mimotope Peptide In Situ in Real Time at a Buried Interface.
papers.authors: Wu G, Qin X, Fathi F, Chen X, Yuan K, Wu Y, Sarker P, Zeng X, Wei T, Chen Z.
papers.abstract: Bioanalytical platforms, such as biosensors and biochips, are widely used for detecting biomolecules including antibodies. Determining the conformation and orientation of antibodies captured by surface-immobilized recognition elements is essential for designing biosensors and biochips with improved performance. However, obtaining such structural information remains challenging because antibodies are located at buried solid/liquid interfaces that are difficult to characterize. Here, we investigated the binding interaction between Herceptin (trastuzumab), a therapeutic monoclonal antibody, and CH19, a HER2 mimotope peptide immobilized at a buried solid/liquid interface. Sum frequency generation (SFG) vibrational spectroscopy revealed specific binding of Herceptin to the surface-immobilized CH19 peptide, whereas no detectable interaction was observed for the non-target antibodies Cetuximab and Rituximab. By integrating SFG measurements with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and one-exciton Hamiltonian spectral calculations, we determined the interfacial molecular structure of Herceptin and found that the antibody adopts a lying-down orientation on the CH19-functionalized surface. These combined experimental and computational results demonstrate that CH19-Herceptin recognition at the interface differs fundamentally from the corresponding interaction in solution, highlighting the unique influence of interfacial environment on antibody-antigen recognition. Our results support a surface-enabled multivalent binding model, in which multiple immobilized CH19 peptides interact with broader regions of Herceptin and generate a contact pattern distinct from that in solution. These results demonstrate that the combined SFG, MD, and spectral-calculation approach can determine the molecular structure of a full-length antibody at a buried interface, offering valuable insights for the rational design of biosensors, biochips, and other surface-based biorecognition analytical technologies.

papers.title: Adaptive Integrated Microfluidic System with Real-Time Dielectric Feedback for Deterministic Micro-Manipulation.
papers.authors: Zhang Y, Guo Z, Yang L, Li Z, Zhang Z, Geng W, Ji Z, Wang R, He J, Chou X.
papers.abstract: Conventional microfluidic particle sorting systems predominantly rely on static, open-loop operational principles, rendering them highly vulnerable to performance deterioration induced by cellular phenotypic heterogeneity and localized hydrodynamic fluctuations. Here, we introduce an adaptive integrated microfluidic system (AIMS) that implements a closed-loop sensing-decision-actuation-verification control framework via on-chip integration of dual-frequency impedance cytometry (IFC) and tunable traveling surface acoustic waves (T-TSAW). An upstream IFC array (1#IFC) performs real-time, label-free electrical interrogation of single-cell dielectric phenotypes. These transient signals are processed in real time by a custom finite-state machine (FSM) algorithm to dynamically modulate the downstream T-TSAW field. Concurrently, a downstream IFC array (2#IFC) performs post-sorting verification and feeds real-time state metrics back to the FSM core. This initiates an adaptive hill-climbing optimization loop to enable continuous acoustic frequency calibration. The system performance was rigorously evaluated using monodisperse polystyrene microspheres and biologically relevant colloidal models. The closed-loop architecture successfully isolated target MCF-7 cells from an erythrocyte-dominated simplified blood model, achieving an acoustic sorting efficiency of 95 ± 1.5% and a purity of 94 ± 2.5%. Furthermore, continuous adaptive sorting of primary mouse immune cell populations (PBMCs and neutrophils) was demonstrated, achieving a sorting efficiency of 92 ± 1.8% and a purity of 93 ± 6.7%. Ultimately, the seamless integration of transient electronic sensing algorithms with multiphysics mechanical actuation establishes a highly robust architectural framework for autonomous microelectromechanical manipulation platforms.

papers.title: A High-Throughput Chemical Proteomic Approach for Profiling Serum CA19-9 Protein Carriers and Their Characterization in Patients with Elevated CA19-9 Levels.
papers.authors: Chen J, Lv Y, Wang H, Wu Z, He A, Liu Y, Yang Y, Gao W, Xu R, Tian R.
papers.abstract: Although the carbohydrate biomarker CA19-9 is widely used for cancer screening, its diagnostic specificity is severely compromised by false-positive elevations in benign inflammatory conditions. Characterizing specific CA19-9 protein carriers provides a promising alternative, yet high-throughput, micro-volume profiling directly from serum remains a challenge. Here, we present a 96-well chemical proteomic platform for the high-throughput profiling of CA19-9-modified proteins. Utilizing a tailored trifunctional chemical probe, photo-activated covalent crosslinking between anti-CA19-9 antibodies and target carriers enables high-stringency enrichment within streptavidin-coated microplates. The workflow identified 509 carriers in cancer cell lines and achieved highly sensitive quantification of established targets, including CD44, LGALS3BP, and mucin family, using as little as 10 μL serum. Notably, this represents the first mass spectrometry-based direct identification of mucin family in peripheral serum. In a clinical cohort of 91 hyper-CA19-9 individuals, CA19-9-modified CD44 was enriched in healthy controls, whereas CA19-9-modified MUC5B was significantly elevated in benign lesions over colorectal cancer (CRC), validated by ELISA across two independent cohorts with AUCs 0.715 and 0.756. Integrating the protein carrier dataset into a random forest machine learning classifier effectively discriminated CRC from benign lesions with an AUC of 0.864. Furthermore, comparative sub-analysis resolved a critical clinical dilemma by identifying 59 upregulated protein carriers in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma relative to benign gallstone-induced cholangitis. Overall, this 96-well chemical proteomic strategy enables parallelized isolation of CA19-9 modified proteins from low-volume samples, establishing a reproducible and scalable tool for the differential profiling of clinically relevant carbohydrate antigen carriers.

papers.title: Androgen receptor signaling at the tumor-immune interface in castration-resistant prostate cancer: single-cell transcriptomic analysis with AR-V7-related RT-qPCR context.
papers.authors: Guo C, Wu L, Xu L.
papers.abstract: Background Androgen receptor splice-variant 7 (AR-V7) is associated with treatment resistance in castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC), whereas its relationship with the tumor-immune microenvironment remains incompletely defined. Methods We performed secondary scRNA-seq analysis of the public CRPC dataset GSE137829 using Seurat-based preprocessing, dimensionality reduction, cell annotation, trajectory inference, SCENIC analysis, pathway enrichment analysis, and CellPhoneDB analysis. Because the public dataset does not provide validated AR-V7 status at the patient or single-cell level, it was not used for AR-V7-positive versus AR-V7-negative classification. RT-qPCR in 22Rv1 and LNCaP cells was retained as supportive analysis of selected AR-associated genes. Results The single-cell dataset demonstrated substantial epithelial, immune, and stromal heterogeneity in CRPC and supported analysis of AR-associated transcriptional states and candidate regulatory programs. RT-qPCR showed higher KLK3, STEAP2, HOXB13, and NKX3-1 expression in 22Rv1 than in LNCaP cells; these differences are interpreted as supportive AR-associated observations rather than AR-V7-specific mechanistic validation. Conclusion The revised study provides an exploratory transcriptomic characterization of AR-associated cellular states in CRPC. The findings are hypothesis-generating and do not establish AR-V7-specific causality or clinical prediction. Functional perturbation studies and datasets with directly measured AR-V7 status are required.

papers.title: Impaired ex vivo T-cell expansion before leukapheresis is associated with out-of-specification tisagenlecleucel manufacturing in pediatric CD19 + ALL.
papers.authors: Bremm M, Heinze G, Schneeberger L, Salzmann-Manrique E, Banisharif Dehkordi J, Peinelt A, Kalwak K, Mielcarek-Siedziuk M, Meisel R, Beier R, Rossig C, Jarisch A, Schlueter J, Rettinger E, Klusmann JH, Cappel C, Bader P, Huenecke S.
papers.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy requires individual production for each patient, starting with a heterogeneous apheresis product of variable cellular composition and function. This inter-patient variability presents a major challenge for standardizing manufacturing processes and may lead to delays or even production failure. The primary aim of this study was to identify pre-leukapheresis characteristics associated with subsequent manufacturing deviations. Multiple T cell-related parameters including T cell receptor (TCR) Vβ repertoire, differentiation status, proliferation capacity (e.g. fraction diluted - DIL), and exhaustion were examined in n = 27 patients before leukapheresis for Kymriah® immunotherapy. These parameters were analyzed for associations with manufacturing specification compliance and out-of-specification (OOS) events. Impaired T-cell proliferation was the parameter most strongly associated with manufacturing specification non-conformance. Six of 21 evaluable patients showed poor proliferation (DIL <80%), including all four patients with OOS manufacturing outcomes. In contrast, all remaining patients had DIL values ≥84.9%. Exploratory associations between selected TCR Vβ subsets and manufacturing specifications were also identified. DIL was the parameter most strongly associated with manufacturing specification compliance and may represent a simple functional measure of pre-apheresis T-cell fitness.

papers.title: Integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analyses reveal UTF1-associated spermatogenic dysfunction and identify ACTRT2 and AKAP4 as biomarkers in non-obstructive azoospermia.
papers.authors: Yu J, Li M, Zhou Y, Liu H, Pei C, Ma L.
papers.abstract: Introduction Non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA) is a severe male infertility disorder caused by spermatogenic failure, and UTF1 is critical for maintaining undifferentiated spermatogonia and regulating germ cell development. This study aimed to explore the role of UTF1-related spermatogenic dysfunction in NOA and identify potential diagnostic biomarkers. Methods We integrated NOA transcriptomic datasets with single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data from Utf1 conditional knockout and normal mouse testes. Bioinformatic analyses and machine learning were applied to screen biomarkers, while functional enrichment, immune infiltration, cell-cell communication, and pseudotime trajectory analyses were performed together with histological validation in Utf1-deficient testes. Results Spermatogonia, Sertoli cells, and spermatids were identified as key cell populations. ACTRT2 and AKAP4 were confirmed as consistently downregulated NOA biomarkers and were integrated into a well-calibrated nomogram. These two genes were associated with cytoskeletal remodeling and meiotic regulation. NOA was also characterized by altered immune infiltration and cell-cell communication, whereas Utf1 deficiency impaired testicular development and spermatogenesis. Discussion Collectively, UTF1 deficiency was closely associated with spermatogenic dysfunction and microenvironmental remodeling in NOA, while ACTRT2 and AKAP4 might serve as potential diagnostic biomarkers of this process. These findings provide new insights into the molecular basis of NOA and may support future disease stratification and targeted intervention strategies.

papers.title: Machine learning-based assessment of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes in breast cancer histopathology: a systematic review and evidence-gap analysis of translational readiness.
papers.authors: Dunenova G, Sarsembayev A, Oshibayeva A, Kyrykbayeva S, Abdrakhmanova Z, Omarova B, Ivankov A, Ualiyeva A, Zhakypova B, Zhagiparova Z, Nuskabayeva G, Suleimenova M, Glushkova N.
papers.abstract: Background Machine learning-based assessment of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) has been proposed to improve the reproducibility and clinical utility of immune-contexture evaluation in breast cancer histopathology. However, existing studies differ substantially in task definition, annotation strategy, model architecture, validation design, and clinical endpoint. This systematic review and evidence-gap analysis aimed to map the translational readiness of TIL-related machine learning studies in breast cancer histopathology and to identify cluster-specific methodological gaps. Methods A systematic search of PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar was conducted up to 20 April 2026, supplemented by backward citation tracing and a targeted Google search of the 30 most relevant additional results. Eligible studies included breast cancer histopathology-based machine learning, deep learning, artificial intelligence, or computational image-analysis studies evaluating TILs or TIL-related immune-cell features. Studies were grouped by principal application into detection/classification, outcome prognostication, and treatment-response prediction. Extracted variables included data source, specimen type, model family, annotation strategy, validation design, clinical comparator use, calibration, decision-curve analysis, incremental value, reproducibility, and methodological challenges. Because of heterogeneity in endpoints and performance metrics, synthesis was descriptive and evidence-map based. Results The primary evidence map included 51 histopathology-image studies: 19 detection/classification, 18 outcome prognostication, and 14 treatment-response prediction studies. External validation was reported in 31.6% of detection/classification studies, 61.1% of prognostication studies, and 57.1% of treatment-response prediction studies. Clinical comparator reporting increased across the same continuum, from 63.2% to 94.4% and 92.9%, respectively. However, calibration was reported in only one prognostication study (5.6%) and in no detection/classification or treatment-response prediction studies. Decision-curve analysis was similarly limited to one prognostication study. Class imbalance was near-universal (94.7-100% across clusters). Scanner/stain robustness was addressed in a majority of studies (63.2-83.3%), but fairness or subgroup analyses remained inconsistently reported (27.8-57.1%). Conclusions TIL machine learning in breast cancer is technically active but clinically under-validated. Future studies should move beyond model development toward externally validated, calibrated, clinically benchmarked, reproducible, and decision-relevant evidence, using cluster-specific planning standards for detection, prognostication, and treatment-response prediction.
