papers.title: Integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analyses suggest a myeloid-associated candidate role of THBS1 in sepsis.
papers.authors: Chen C, Jin Y, Chen W, Yuan H, Hu Y, Hu J.
papers.abstract: Background Sepsis remains a major cause of mortality worldwide, and biomarkers that integrate inflammatory dysregulation, immune-cell localization, and prognostic relevance remain limited. To identify a candidate molecule linked to myeloid immune responses in sepsis, we performed an integrated analysis of public bulk transcriptomic datasets, single-cell RNA sequencing data, a small exploratory clinical RNA-sequencing cohort, and compound screening analyses. Results Differential expression analysis and meta-analysis across public datasets identified THBS1 as a consistently altered transcript in sepsis. In a small exploratory peripheral-blood transcriptomic cohort comprising 23 patients with sepsis and 10 healthy controls, THBS1 was selected for downstream analysis on the basis of its position in the public-data protein-protein interaction network and the subsequent THBS1 -focused analyses. The reused clinical RNA-sequencing cohort was retained only as an exploratory description and was not used to claim independent validation. Single-cell analysis suggested that THBS1 expression was more prominent in subsets of myeloid-related cell populations. Survival analysis in an external dataset indicated that high THBS1 expression was associated with poorer outcomes, but this finding should be interpreted as exploratory because formal adjustment for disease severity was not possible. Candidate compounds associated with THBS1 were further prioritized by database mining and molecular docking. Conclusions This study provides transcriptomic and computational evidence suggesting that THBS1 may be associated with myeloid-related immune activity and adverse prognosis in sepsis. Because the clinical cohort was small, protein-level validation and functional experiments were not performed, and substantial heterogeneity was observed across public datasets, these findings should be interpreted as preliminary and hypothesis-generating.

papers.title: Microglia in Alzheimer's disease: from pathogenic mechanisms to therapeutic targeting.
papers.authors: Tang L, Li XY, Ran Z, Qin ZZ, Chen SY, Zhang MM, Zhou LY, Wang WJ, Chen L.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a multifactorial neurodegenerative disorder driven by β-amyloid (Aβ) deposition, tau hyperphosphorylation, synaptic dysfunction, neuroinflammation, vascular injury, and metabolic dysregulation. Recent advances in single-cell, spatial, and multi-omics transcriptomics have substantially reshaped our understanding of microglia, shifting the field from the classical M1/M2-like polarization dichotomy toward a model of state-dependent functional heterogeneity. Distinct subpopulations-including disease-associated microglia, lipid-associated microglia, interferon-responsive microglia, and senescence-associated microglia are now mechanistically linked to Aβ clearance, tau propagation, complement-mediated synaptic pruning, NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome activation, and immunometabolic reprogramming. Central to this regulatory network are the TREM2-ApoE axis, complement cascades, NLRP3 inflammasome, mitochondrial dysfunction, and aberrant lipid/iron metabolism, which largely contribute to AD progression. In parallel, the clinical deployment of anti-Aβ monoclonal antibodies such as lecanemab has ushered in the era of disease-modifying therapy; however, limited efficacy and the occurrence of amyloid-related imaging abnormalities underscore that Aβ removal alone is insufficient to halt disease evolution completely. In this review, we systematically synthesize the evolving landscape of microglial states and their pathogenic contributions, and we further evaluate current therapeutic avenues, including microglia-targeted strategies, anti-Aβ antibody combination regimens, non-pharmacological interventions, and peripheral immunomodulation. We also compare these microglial mechanisms with those in multiple sclerosis to highlight shared neuroimmune modules and disease-specific features. Our goal is to provide a valuable updated reference for accurate molecular subtyping and multi-target combination therapy in AD.

papers.title: Targeting the microglia-synapse interface in depression: molecular mechanisms and pharmacological perspectives from traditional Chinese medicine.
papers.authors: Yao SX, Xu ZY, Zhao HQ, Deng DF, Yang Y, Tang L, Tan H, Liu J.
papers.abstract: Depression is a prevalent neuropsychiatric disorder characterized by impaired synaptic plasticity, disrupted neural circuits, and persistent neuroimmune dysregulation. Increasing evidence indicates that microglia-mediated synaptic pruning, a physiological process essential for neural circuit refinement, becomes abnormally activated under depressive conditions, leading to excessive synaptic elimination and impaired connectivity. Complement-dependent pathways, inflammatory signaling, mitochondrial dysfunction, and alterations in the neural microenvironment contribute to microglial activation and synaptic remodeling. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM), with its multi-component and multi-target properties, has shown potential antidepressant effects by regulating neuroinflammation, immune homeostasis, and synaptic plasticity. This review summarizes recent advances in microglia-mediated synaptic pruning in depression and discusses the potential role of TCM interventions in this neuroimmune pathway. Current studies suggest that stress-induced microenvironmental changes promote microglial activation and excessive synaptic engulfment, while TCM formulas, herbal extracts, and bioactive compounds may restore synaptic function by modulating microglial polarization, inflammatory responses, complement signaling, and mitochondrial homeostasis. However, direct evidence demonstrating the regulation of microglia-mediated synaptic pruning by TCM remains limited. Future research integrating single-cell sequencing, advanced imaging, and molecular tracing approaches is required to clarify these mechanisms. Overall, targeting microglial synaptic remodeling provides a promising framework for understanding depression pathogenesis and developing novel TCM-based therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Spectral flow cytometry for high-dimensional immune profiling: from technological advances to multimodal precision immunology.
papers.authors: Zhu Y, Li J, Li C, Yu M, Liu A, Zhang Q, Xie Y, Chen K.
papers.abstract: Spectral flow cytometry has emerged as a powerful high-dimensional platform for resolving immune heterogeneity and functional states at the single-cell level. By capturing the full emission spectra of fluorophores and applying computational spectral unmixing, it expands the multiparameter profiling capacity of conventional flow cytometry and enables more comprehensive characterization of immune cell phenotypes and functional states. In this review, we summarize the technological evolution of spectral flow cytometry and discuss how spectral acquisition and computational unmixing support multidimensional analysis of immune composition, cellular states, and functional programs. We then examine its applications in immune ecosystem mapping, tumor immunology, immune development and regeneration, vaccination, autoimmune diseases, and translational immune monitoring, with particular emphasis on biomarker discovery, disease stratification, therapeutic response assessment, and precision immunology. We further discuss the integration of spectral flow cytometry with mass cytometry, artificial intelligence, single-cell transcriptomics and proteomics, spatial profiling, imaging technologies, and functional assays. These multimodal approaches provide complementary phenotypic, molecular, spatial, and functional information, creating opportunities for more comprehensive reconstruction of immune ecosystems and deeper interpretation of cellular states. Despite these advances, challenges remain in standardization and cross-platform reproducibility, autofluorescence management, high-dimensional data analysis, and clinical validation. Future development will therefore require not only continued advances in spectral acquisition and computational analysis but also harmonized workflows, robust analytical frameworks, and effective multimodal integration. Overall, spectral flow cytometry is evolving from a high-parameter immunophenotyping technology into a scalable platform for ecosystem-level immune profiling, providing an important bridge between cellular phenotyping, mechanistic discovery, biomarker development, and precision immunology.

papers.title: Natural killer cells in colorectal cancer liver metastasis: redefining immune surveillance and plasticity.
papers.authors: Lu Y, Xia C, Gu J.
papers.abstract: Natural killer (NK) cells are key effectors in innate immunity and serve as early responders against disseminated tumor cells. In colorectal cancer liver metastasis (CRLM), the liver's unique immune landscape presents both challenges and opportunities for NK cell-mediated tumor control. While NK cells have long been considered uniform cytotoxic sentinels, recent studies have reshaped this view by uncovering a diverse spectrum of NK cell states with distinct migratory, transcriptional, and functional programs. These findings reveal a heterogeneous NK-cell compartment in the metastatic liver shaped by tissue context and microenvironmental cues, with distinct residency-associated and functional programs. Advances in high-dimensional single-cell technologies have accelerated the characterization of NK cell heterogeneity, plasticity, and interactions within the metastatic niche. In this review, we summarize recent insights into the evolving roles of NK cells in CRLM, highlighting how they contribute to immune surveillance, niche remodeling, and potential therapeutic modulation.

figure.caption: Rewriting NK immune surveillance in CRLM: from uniform killers to state-based control. NK cells provide rapid innate immune surveillance by integrating activating and inhibitory signals to execute cytotoxic programs and coordinate downstream immunity. In the liver, however, immune tolerance, metabolic specialization, continuous antigen exposure, and spatial compartmentalization reshape NK differentiation and function. In CRLM, NK responses are therefore best understood through a state-based framework in which distinct NK states coexist and immune control depends on which functional programs dominate and where they operate within metastatic lesions.

papers.title: Novel compound heterozygous mutations of DOCK2 associated with early-onset recurrent infections.
papers.authors: Yang Z, Wang L, Wang Y, Zhu X, Huang Y, Luo Y, Yang J, He T.
papers.abstract: Introduction Dedicator of cytokinesis 2 (DOCK2) deficiency is a rare combined immunodeficiency characterized by defects in both cellular and humoral immunity and caused by pathogenic mutations in the DOCK2 gene. Herein, we report a 3-year-8-month-old Chinese girl presenting with recurrent infections, immune thrombocytopenia (ITP), elevated IgE levels, and a hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH)-like episode to broaden the clinical phenotype spectrum of the DOCK2 defect. Methods All tests and molecular genetic analyses were performed after obtaining informed consent from the parents. Demographic, clinical, and laboratory findings were abstracted from outpatient and inpatient encounters. Whole-exome sequencing (WES) was performed on peripheral blood cells to identify the genetic etiology, followed by immunological evaluation (including lymphocyte subset analysis, T-cell receptor Vβ repertoire analysis, and neutrophil oxidative function assays) and in silico prediction. Sanger sequencing was used to confirm the identified variants. Results WES identified two novel compound heterozygous variants in DOCK2 (c. 106 C>T, p.R36X and c. 2150T>C, p.L717P), each inherited from one parent. Immunological evaluation revealed combined immune defects involving T cells and B cells, including reduced T/B cell subsets, skewed TCR repertoire, and impaired T cell proliferation. In silico analyses indicated that the variants affect highly conserved residues and are predicted to disrupt protein structure. The patient received supportive treatment, regular intravenous immunoglobulin replacement therapy, and sulfonamide prophylaxis, resulting in effective disease control. Discussion This case expands the genotypic and phenotypic spectrum of DOCK2 deficiency and highlights its critical role in human immune regulation. It also underscores the importance of early genetic diagnosis to guide timely clinical management. However, functional validation experiments were not performed to further confirm the pathogenicity of the identified variants, and additional protein expression studies are warranted.

papers.title: Subtype or state? Rethinking the apCAF paradox and fibroblast plasticity in gastrointestinal cancers.
papers.authors: Yu Z, Hu D, An Z.
papers.abstract: Antigen-presenting cancer-associated fibroblasts (apCAFs), commonly defined by MHC class II molecules, CD74, and related transcriptional programs, exhibit divergent functions across gastrointestinal tumors. In pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, mesothelium-derived apCAFs promote regulatory T-cell differentiation and suppress effector responses, whereas their abundance in gastric cancer is associated with earlier-stage disease, longer survival, and improved immunotherapy responses. This paradox may reflect microenvironmental context and classifications that conflate transcriptional state, cellular origin, and immune function. apCAFs may therefore represent reversible, context-dependent states defined by origin, MHC class II-restricted antigen presentation, and co-stimulatory capacity. We propose a two-layer model that has not been validated in apCAFs. In this model, the chromatin accessibility of CIITA, CD40, CD80, and CD86 constructs a functional licensing range, while interferon - γ (IFN - γ), interleukin-1 (IL-1), and transforming growth factor - β (TGF - β) guide the formation of specific phenotypes within this range. Insufficient co-stimulation may favor immune tolerance; activation of co-stimulatory programs may support CD4 + T-cell help and CD8 + T-cell infiltration. Treatment-induced changes in CAF composition may reflect selective survival or genuine state transitions. Distinguishing these mechanisms requires lineage tracing, longitudinal single-cell transcriptomic and chromatin profiling, and patient-derived organoid-fibroblast co-cultures. Neoadjuvant therapy and serial endoscopic sampling provide feasible settings for capturing transient states. This framework supports replacing broad CAF depletion with temporally and state-informed functional reprogramming.

Fibroblasts from different sources, including resident tissue fibroblasts, mesothelial cells and stellate cells, tend to be MHC class II molecule positive phenotypes (upper left and center). papers.title: Engineering aptamer-based therapeutics for precision cancer immunotherapy: from molecular targeting to clinical applications.
papers.authors: Azhar MA, Ahmed S, Altuhami A, Shabab M, Assiri AM, Broering DC, Mir TA.
papers.abstract: Although cancer immunotherapy has revolutionized cancer therapy, the clinical efficacy of this approach is restricted due to tumor heterogeneity, immune escape, therapeutic resistance, poor tumor penetration, and toxic side effects. Short single-stranded DNA or RNA oligonucleotides, termed aptamers, have high affinity for a given target, low immunogenicity, and high chemical programmability and are emerging as promising agents for precision cancer therapies and immuno-oncology. This review aims to provide a comprehensive, integrated overview of the development of aptamer-based cancer therapeutics, from molecular engineering and pharmacology to clinical applications and translational potential. The discovery and optimization of tumor and immune-specific aptamers have been enhanced by the development of conventional SELEX, Cell-SELEX, in vivo SELEX, high-throughput sequencing, microfluidic selection, and AI-assisted selection. To enhance nuclease resistance, circulation time, biodistribution, and tumor accumulation, chemical modifications such as PEGylation, 2'-fluoro, 2'-O-methyl, LNAs, phosphorothioate linkages, circularization, and lipid/albumin binding have been developed. Aptamers can directly regulate oncogenic and immune signaling pathways or be used as targeted delivery vehicles for chemotherapeutic drugs, siRNAs, miRNAs, proteins, peptides, and CRISPR-based systems. Moreover, aptamers targeting tumor-associated biomarkers, cancer stem cells, the tumor vasculature, stromal components, and immune regulatory pathways have the potential to selectively remodel the tumor microenvironment. In addition, they are well-suited to other immunotherapy strategies, including immune checkpoint inhibitors, chemotherapy, radiotherapy, photodynamic or photothermal therapy, oncolytic viruses, and cancer vaccines, thereby further supporting a multifunctional, personalized treatment approach. Although there has been significant progress in pre-clinical research, several issues remain regarding pharmacokinetics, tumor penetration, off-target effects, manufacturing, long-term safety, regulatory approval, and clinical validation. Additional advancements in aptamer engineering, nanotechnology, computational design, and biomarker-directed therapy could potentially enable the development of these platforms into successful next-generation precision cancer immunotherapies.

papers.title: GlycoStamp-seq: Single-cell nascent sialoglycometabolomics captures sialylation dynamics in immune cells of an oxaliplatin-treated bladder cancer mouse model.
papers.authors: Wu X, Zhao Z, Ouyang S, Hao X, Li J, Zhu W, Zhang T, Lu S, Dong T, Jiang N, Yang X, Guo H, Li JP, Tian T, Yang R.
papers.abstract: Dynamic remodeling of immune cell-surface glycans reflects cellular state and immune activity. Despite advances in single-cell glyco-profiling, current methods primarily capture pre-existing glycan epitopes, providing limited information on dynamic sialoglycans. Here, we present GlycoStamp-seq, a method to profile nascent sialoglycan dynamics by coupling Ac₄ManNAz-based metabolic glycoengineering with single-cell RNA/TCR sequencing (scRNA/TCR-seq) and scDyna-seq. We apply GlycoStamp-seq by injecting Ac₄ManNAz into oxaliplatin-treated mice with subcutaneous bladder tumors, days before extracting tumor-derived single-cell suspensions for sequencing. Following oxaliplatin treatment, a subset of CD8⁺ T cells in the tumor immune microenvironment exhibits elevated nascent sialoglycan activity, enhanced effector programs, and increased clonal expansion. Furthermore, elevated nascent sialoglycan levels mark antigen-reactive CD8⁺ T cells with increased anti-tumor efficacy in vitro and in vivo. GlycoStamp-seq may thus serve as a versatile platform for profiling nascent sialoglycan dynamics in complex tissues, thereby expanding the single-cell multi-omics toolkit and providing insights into sialoglycan dynamics during therapeutic response.

papers.title: Microbial ecological instability and non-linear host interactions shape airway inflammation in HIV-associated COPD.

papers.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is increasingly recognized among people living with HIV in sub-Saharan Africa, yet the mechanisms linking airway microbial ecology to chronic inflammation remain poorly understood. Here, we study 200 adults stratified by HIV and COPD status, including 160 participants with two-year longitudinal follow-up, using an integrated multi-omics framework combining sputum 16S rRNA profiling, bacterial outer membrane vesicle quantification, airway cytokine profiling, CyTOF immune phenotyping, bulk transcriptomics of induced sputum, bronchoalveolar lavage and peripheral blood, and bronchoalveolar lavage single-cell RNA sequencing-guided deconvolution. We find that sputum microbial communities are shaped predominantly by temporal ecological turnover rather than HIV or COPD status. Although microbial diversity, microbiome instability, outer membrane vesicle burden and inferred airway cellular composition remain largely preserved, HIV-associated COPD exhibits disease-specific microbial signatures together with inflammatory transcriptional remodeling concentrated in induced sputum. Integrated analyses identify selective host-microbe interaction networks linking discrete microbial taxa with inflammatory, immune and transcriptional programmes.

papers.title: A progenitor-exhausted (Tpex)-like CD8 + T-cell compartment extends across axillary lymphatic basin beyond sentinel lymph nodes in breast cancer.
papers.authors: Li S, Liu B, Yang L, Wang C, Du W, Zhang S, Gao R, Zhang J, Li H, Li Y, Chen Y, Liu M, Qi H, Wang S.
papers.abstract: Objective The immunological consequences of sparing uninvolved axillary lymph nodes (LNs) in breast cancer remain unclear. We asked whether a transcriptomically defined progenitor-exhausted-like (Tpex-like) CD8 + T-cell compartment is confined to the sentinel node or distributed across the axillary basin. Methods We integrated single-cell transcriptomics, paired T-cell receptor (TCR) profiling, and complementary flow cytometry across 15 patients (163,600 cells). We characterized Tpex-like CD8 + T cell populations and assessed their distribution, clonal expansion, and TCR clonotype sharing across sentinel and downstream non-sentinel uninvolved lymph nodes. Complementary flow cytometry was performed to evaluate progenitor-associated T-cell phenotypes at the protein level. Results Uninvolved LNs were enriched for a C00 Tpex-like cluster characterized by relative enrichment of progenitor-associated TCF7 together with partial exhaustion-lineage features, including TOX expression and TCF7-TOX co-detection, but sparse PDCD1 transcript detection. C00 clonotypes were shared with tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes, whereas metastatic involvement was associated with reduced representation of this compartment. C00 abundance and clonotype-associated properties showed no clear positional differences across sentinel and downstream non-sentinel uninvolved nodes. Independently, flow cytometry detected TCF7/PD-1/TOX progenitor-like phenotypes in downstream non-sentinel uninvolved nodes from five patients; these protein-defined populations were not assumed to be identical to C00. Conclusions Anatomically distinct uninvolved axillary LNs contain a broadly distributed transcriptomically defined C00 Tpex-like compartment, with complementary protein-level evidence for TCF7 + PD-1 + TOX + progenitor-like phenotypes. These findings provide a biological framework for considering the immune architecture preserved by axillary de-escalation.
